News.title: Mystery as goth influencer, 30, and boyfriend shot dead with their bodies found on rural road after being held captive
News.content:
SAVAGE END Mystery as goth influencer, 30, and boyfriend shot dead with their bodies found on rural road after being held captive

A GOTH influencer and her boyfriend have been shot dead as cops say they may have been held captive for drug debts.

Ulissias Marcelli, 30, and her partner Vinícius Souza de Carvalho, 28, were found with gunshot wounds on a roadside in Porto Seguro, northeast Brazil.



The pair had been dead for around a day when they were discovered on the rural road by a farmer on Friday night.

Cops have now launched a probe into the mystery killing – with initial leads suggesting the pair may have had ties with local drug cartels.



Officers told Brazilian newspaper G1 that the former beauty queen and her boyfriend may have been held captive before they were gunned down.

Cops added that they were investigating alleged debt linked to drug trafficking or to a possible sale of narcotics.

Forensic teams recovered seven spent bullet casings and seized Ulissia’s phone for analysis – that of her partner’s was missing.

No suspects have been announced and the motive for the murder has not yet been established.

The self-proclaimed “Miss Tattoo” was a fire dancer who posted content about rock music, motorcycles and animal welfare to her more than 20,000 followers.

Ulissias also leaves behind a 13-year-old son.



Both Ulissias and her boyfriend lived locally and worked in events catering.

The beauty queen’s mother shared her grief, writing: “Go in peace, my loves. You leave an immortal legacy. We will miss you dearly – this is such a heartbreaking loss.”

Ulissias won a local beauty title in 2021 and had been announced as a presenter at Rock Gaya Festival on July 25 – just days before her brutal murder.



The music and arts event posted a tribute to Instagram, writing: “On Thursday, we joyfully shared that Ulissias would be part of the Rock Gaya Festival as one of our presenters. Today, with profound sadness, we say goodbye to her presence among us.

“We are still trying to find words for a moment like this. It’s hard to believe that someone who was about to share such a special moment with us has left us so soon.”

Fans have shared an outpouring of grief on social media.

One wrote: “My deepest condolences to the whole family and to the son.”

“Brazil is experiencing rampant violence; my condolences to the family members”, added another.



The police have not yet arrested any suspects.

News.title: Boy, 15, charged with raping and sexually assaulting eight girls aged between 10 and 15
News.content:
RAPE PROBE Boy, 15, charged with raping and sexually assaulting eight girls aged between 10 and 15

A 15-YEAR-old boy has been charged with raping and sexually assaulting eight girls between the ages of 10 and 15.

The teenager, who cannot be named because of his age, allegedly committed the offences between 2023 and 2025.



He was charged with numerous offences including raping a girl under 13, making an indecent photograph or pseudo-photograph of a child, and sexual assault.

District Judge Amar Mehta told the boy: “Your case is too serious to be tried in this court.



“Therefore it’s going to be tried at the Crown Court at Northampton.

“I’m going to send your case to Northampton Crown Court for another hearing similar to this one.”



The teen was accompanied by his mother to Wellingborough Youth Court on Tuesday.

He was not asked to enter the dock and took a seat at the back of the court room.

The boy was charged with 22 offences related to rape and sexual assault against eight victims who were aged between 10 and 15 at the time.

He was not asked to enter any pleas during the 20-minute hearing.



The court heard he was being charged with 12 counts of sexually assaulting a female, three counts of assaulting a girl under 13 by touching, and one count of raping a girl under 13.

As well, he is facing charges of one count of assaulting a female aged 13 and over by penetration with a part of the body or thing, one count of raping a girl aged 13-15, and two counts of making an indecent photograph or pseudo-photograph of a child.

He is also being charged with possessing a prohibited image of a child and another of possessing extreme pornographic images.

Following the decision by District Judge Mehta to have the boy tried at a crown court, he will next appear on August 18.

The judge granted him a conditional bail, instructing him not to contact the alleged victims.



He was also told to have no unsupervised contact with females under 16 and to engage with the Northamptonshire Youth Justice Service.

During the hearing, the boy spoke only to confirm his name, date of birth and address, and to ask the judge what the Youth Justice Service was.

News.title: Watch as defiant drivers flout warnings to cross COLLAPSED bridge
News.content:
THIS is the dramatic moment a car crossed a river, using a buckled bridge in Greece to save 20 minutes on their commute.

Footage shows the vehicle on the out-of-service link – its midpoint only a few inches above Pineios River in central Greece.



Three years after Storm Daniel tore through the country, as well as Turkey and Bulgaria, Palaiopyrgos Bridge in Larissa remains heavily damaged.

The bridge once linked coastal communities in the municipalities of Agia and Tempe, but its collapse has disrupted local travel.



While considered unsafe, drivers continue to take the risk to avoid taking another, 19-mile longer route using the national highway.

Yiannis Beritzas, the president of the Paleopyrgos village, said the bridge has cut off direct routes to Mount Kissavos.



“What should we do? Should we go all the way around?” one local told Skai.

“Where should we go? Nothing can be done. We play with death every day.”

The situation becomes even more dangerous when the level of the Pinios River rises and the waters pass over the crumbled bridge.

The Palaiopyrgos Bridge is among the infrastructure that has not been repaired yet.



Although the contract for the construction of a new bridge has already been signed by a well-known construction group, the project has not yet started.

“All traffic is at risk,” said the president of the Paleopyrgos Agricultural Cooperative, Thanos Hatzizogidis.

“Let’s not find ourselves running behind the events again. Large and loaded vehicles are passing by, while there is not even the necessary traffic lights.”



The catastrophic floods caused by the storm in 2023 resulted in around $2.14 billion worth of damage.

In Greece, 17 people died because of the storm, which at the time was described as a “biblical catastrophe”.

Five people were also killed in Turkey during the floods, while at least two victims were found in Bulgaria.

News.title: PC Andrew Harper’s killers ‘set for early release’ under Labour scheme as his mum furious over ‘insult beyond words’
News.content:
TWO of PC Andrew Harper’s killers could be set for an early release from jail under Labour plans to tackle prison overcrowding, with his furious mother branding it an “insult beyond words”.

Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole were jailed for 13 years in 2020 for the manslaughter of the 28-year-old officer.



The pair, who were 17 at the time of the offense in August 2019, were passengers in the car that dragged PC Harper for more than a mile along country roads when his ankles got caught in a towrope loop.

He had gone to investigate the theft of a quad bike when Bowers and Cole tried to escape in a vehicle driven by a third killer, Henry Long.



PC Harper sustained serious injuries and died in the road.

But the pair are now eligible to be freed just halfway through their sentences under the Ministry of Justice early release scheme.



Debbie Adlam, the police officer’s mother, was told that his killers may have their sentences reduced in a letter from the MoJ.

The heartbroken mother told The Telegraph that the potential early release of the killers was an “insult beyond anything able to be put into words”.

She told the outlet: “It makes me feel sick. Andrew’s life doesn’t get to come back. It feels like a slap in the face and an insult.

“People are getting a free pass for crime in this country. I like to try to be proud of my country, but this isn’t something to be proud of. There’s a lot going wrong.”



It is unclear precisely when Bowers and Cole will become eligible for release, though it could be by the end of the year.

The driver, Long, is not eligible for early release under the scheme and will only be able to seek parole after serving half of his 16-year jail sentence.

The original sentences handed to the trio sparked a national outcry and a campaign for “Harper’s Law”, which introduced a mandatory life sentence for anyone convicted of killing emergency workers while committing a crime.



Led by the officer’s widow, Lissie Harper – who had married him just one month before his death – the campaign was backed by Labour at the time, alongside Tory amendments to enact the legislation.

Frontbenchers Nick Thomas-Symonds and Sarah Jones, now the policing minister, previously met Mrs Harper to offer their support.

The killers’ eligibility for early release will fuel fresh demands for Andy Burnham’s new government to rethink the controversial policy.



Under the scheme, serious criminals – including killers, rapists, and child groomers – are eligible to be freed halfway through their sentences rather than two-thirds, provided they have not committed serious prison rule breaches.

Criminals convicted of less serious offences can be freed as little as a third of the way through.

The scheme is written into law via the 2026 Sentencing Act and is expected to become operational this September, leading to the early release of more than 5,000 offenders over the following 10 months.

Before Mr Burnham became Prime Minister on Monday, sources confirmed he was reviewing whether and how to exempt rapists and child groomers in the face of a growing backlash.

An MoJ spokesman said: “This was a horrific crime, and our deepest sympathies are with Pc Andrew Harper’s family and friends.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“In 2024, the country was facing a prison crisis and a total breakdown of law and order, with judges ordered to stop jailing dangerous criminals.

“This government is committed to public safety: we are building prison places at the fastest rate since the Victorian era, and taking the difficult decisions needed to lock up the most dangerous offenders.”

News.title: Trump will allow Andrew Tate to be extradited to UK after self-proclaimed misogynist ‘raped & choked women unconscious’
News.content:
TATE PROBE Trump will allow Andrew Tate to be extradited to UK after self-proclaimed misogynist ‘raped & choked women unconscious’

DONALD Trump will allow the Tate brothers to be extradited to the UK to face sexual abuse and child pornography charges.

Self-proclaimed misogynist Andrew Tate has been accused of raping and choking women unconscious in Britain and possessing child abuse images.



British detectives demanded the arrests of the suspected rapists after a further four alleged victims came forward in the UK, bringing the total to seven.

The pair were detained in Miami on Saturday as they arrived at a bare-knuckle boxing event.



The Tate brothers’ lawyer Joe McBride slammed the arrests and claimed the duo were victims of a “political witch-hunt”.

He called on Trump to intervene and told reporters outside court that “he was elected to fight against this kind of nonsense”.



Andrew has previously said: “I’m very close with the Trump family. I know them well.”

The brothers had allegedly contacted people close to the president after they were detained – but the White House on Tuesday confirmed they would not step in.

A US Official told The Telegraph: “The White House has no involvement and no feelings on the issue.”

Andrew Tate has previously boasted of his high-powered connections in the US government – claiming that he befriended Trump’s son Barron in July 2024 after an assassination attempt on the president.



And the Financial Times reported that one of Trump’s top envoys had helped him and his brother flee Romania after their arrest last year.

When asked about this bombshell claim, Trump said: “I know nothing about that.”

The brothers, who are dual British-US citizens, face a total of 59 charges in the UK, according to Bedfordshire Police.



The allegations date from between 2010 and 2017 and include rape and sex trafficking.

Andrew faces 32 new charges, including seven relating to rape and 19 involving extreme pornography and indecent images of children.

Tristan, 38, faces six more, including two rape and sex-trafficking charges.

According to unsealed documents, Andrew allegedly repeatedly choked one woman until she passed out and then raped her at her home in Bedford in 2015.

Another woman alleged Andrew visited her Manchester home before choking her to the point that “she was afraid Tate was going to kill her”.



The complaint also alleged that Tristan regularly choked, beat and raped a woman that he was in a romantic relationship in 2012 and 2013.

Both brothers, who are dual US-British citizens, have repeatedly denied any wrongdoing.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Tates were born in the US before moving to Luton as children.



They are now based in Romania, where they were first arrested in 2022.

News.title: Andy Burnham slashes bus fares to £2 across England as new PM makes ‘breathing room’ pledge to hard-up voters
News.content:
BUS fares will be capped at £2 across England from next year, Andy Burnham will announce.

The new PM will lower the current £3 ceiling as part of a cost of living package to give the public more “breathing room”.



As Manchester Mayor he capped fares on his flagship Bee Network to £2 for a single adult fare.

The cap was first brought in nationally at £2 by the Tory government in 2023 but was then raised to £3 in 2024.



The new cap will come in from January.

Mr Burnham has vowed to take “immediate” action to lighten the load on hard-up families before setting out real action at the autumn Budget.



He has admitted his first measures “won’t solve everything” but would be a start on the cost of living.

On Monday, he told his Cabinet that they needed to be a “cost of living government” as he set out his priorities.

As part of his cost-cutting initiative, he has also pledged to slash taxes on electricity bills from October.

With VAT expected to be taken off electricity bills, UK households would see £45 off their annual price cap.



Reducing the tax from 5 per cent to 0 per cent is another move by Mr Burnham to help bring down inflation.

He has said that the policy, costing £850million in 2026/27, will be paid off by cancelling the Digital ID cards scheme.

Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey MP said: “For too long, too many people have struggled with the cost of living.

“Today’s energy tax cut will give families some breathing room on bills, and provide some reassurance this winter.

“This measure is funded this year from cancelling the Digital ID programme, and it will help bring down inflation while supporting households in every postcode.”



But according to Starmer ally, Darren Jones, the Digital ID programme was “unfunded”.

Just after leaving Downing Street from his position as Chief Secretary to the Prime Minister, Mr Jones posted online saying: “Good news that VAT will be cut on electricity bills.

“It’s a simple way for families to save a few quid, and to mechanically help to keep inflation that little bit lower.

“But the DigitalID program was unfunded.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The government will have to set out how it will pay for its new policies at the budget.”



It was not clear where the money to fund the Digital ID programme would come from In the Office for Budget Responsibility’s Economic and Fiscal Outlook from November last year.

News.title: Boozy karaoke, tearful aides checking Cabinet news & Keir T-shirts – what REALLY happened at Starmer’s pub send-off
News.content:
KEIR Starmer’s pub send-off featured boozy karaoke and tearful aides wearing T-shirts supporting their boss, The Sun can reveal.

The ex-PM led the knees-up on Monday alongside his wife Vic, their children, and a tight circle of loyalists in North London.



A number of aides sported custom-made T-shirts featuring the former PM’s face alongside the slogan “Starmer Solid” – the affectionate moniker coined for his fiercest backbench allies.

One woman, pictured next to Sir Keir’s former press aide George Mason, wore a T-shirt with the writing “sparkle with Starmer” on it.



Fresh from the chopping block, former ministers downed glasses of white wine and traded gossip with anxious aides.

And staffers and ex-No 10 officials are understood to have partied well into the night.

Many eventually retreated to the pub’s upstairs karaoke room to belt out their favourite anthems long after their former boss had gone home.

Earlier, attendees were seen frantically refreshing Twitter to see who had seized their former offices in Burnham’s swift reshuffle.



But ex-ministers such as Reeves were largely seen in good spirits, laughing alongside aides as they downed drinks.

“It was a weird mix of anger and sadness”, one person there told The Sun.

“I think everyone was taken aback by just how big and brutal the purge was.”

Another said: “It is a massacre by the Manchester Mafia. They are running No10 now.”

Starmer had made a beeline for a pub in Kentish Town with loyalists including Rachel Reeves hours after handing over the keys to No10 to Burnham.



Before long, a steady stream of the freshly deposed arrived to join the fray which ended up lasting long into the night.

Defeated big hitters including Darren Jones, Jo Stevens, and Richard Hermer all filtered into the pub, each greeted by a wall of cheers from dozens of assembled Labour staffers.

The pub’s walls were plastered with behind-the-scenes photographs capturing Sir Keir’s two tumultuous years in Downing Street, serving as a backdrop to the afternoon’s post-mortem.

As the sun began to fade, Sir Keir made his exit hand-in-hand with Vic, raising a farewell bouquet of flowers high into the air like a trophy to a final round of applause.

But the ex-Prime Minister’s departure did little to stem the revelry as the night ended in boozy karaoke.



Earlier, Sir Keir had delivered a short goodbye speech outside Downing Street and travelled to Buckingham Palace to formally resign to King Charles, ending his two tumultuous years in office.

He said serving as Prime Minister had been “the privilege of my life” and insisted he left office “with good grace and with a smile”.

Sir Keir reflected on taking Labour from its crushing 2019 election defeat to a landslide victory in 2024, declaring: “My work is done.”

Starmer had swept into No10 with a landslide majority in 2024, promising to restore stability after years of Conservative rule.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But less than two years later, his authority had been battered by Peter Mandelson’s appointment as US ambassador, Cabinet resignations and internal Labour rows.



Sir Keir announced he would step aside last month after Mr Burnham’s stonking victory in the Makerfield by-election, which paved the way for his unopposed win in the Labour leadership.

News.title: Pregnant teen, 17, dies hours after planned gender reveal party as heartbroken sister pays tribute to ‘beautiful’ girl
News.content:
TEEN TRAGEDY Pregnant teen, 17, dies hours after planned gender reveal party as heartbroken sister pays tribute to ‘beautiful’ girl

A PREGNANT 17-year-old died just hours after a planned gender reveal party for her unborn child, with her family paying moving tribute.

Summer Rose Miles, 17, collapsed at home in Nottingham on July 9 before being rushed to hospital by air ambulance.



While on life support, on the day her gender reveal celebration was due to take place, she delivered her tiny baby, who was born sleeping.

Summer underwent emergency surgery, but the damage to her brain stem proved too severe.



Her devastated sister, Chloe Jade, paid tribute to the “beautiful” teenager as she launched a GoFundMe page to help their heartbroken parents, Mandy and Scott, cover funeral costs, the Nottingham Post reported.

Summer, from Top Valley, had matured immensely after becoming pregnant and possessed a “different light about her,” her sister told the outlet.

Chloe said: “She loves children so much, and although young, and it was a shock for everyone, we know she’d have been the best mummy ever, and everyone was looking forward to the next chapter.”

Despite initial struggles at school, she excelled in college, where she met her boyfriend and best friend, Carson.

The couple’s gender reveal had been set for July 11 in her family’s garden, with Summer convinced she was expecting a girl.

Chloe told the Nottingham Post: “The gender reveal decorations and plans were all prepped by my mum, following a private scan gifted to her from her boyfriend’s family who would have also attended.



“Unfortunately the scan never had a chance to happen. One of the last things Summer told my mum was that she was thankful for how nice she had made the garden look for her big day outside.”

Doctors described the fatal haemorrhage as “spontaneous, tragic, and exceptionally rare” for a fit and healthy girl of her age, according to her family.

Remembered by loved ones as a “whirlwind of chaos and laughter,” the horse-loving teenager was a self-described “little rebel” who was devoted to her family.

She was particularly close to her mother, Mandy, whom she treated as a best friend, as well as her protective older brother, Jordan, her father, Scott, and her young niece, Ava.

Her family said they know she would have been the “best mummy ever” as they face a tragedy that has left them struggling to comprehend how quickly life has changed.



And while Chloe reflected on the special memories, she and her family are also going through hell, by having to arrange a final farewell for Summer.

Writing an emotional message on the fundraiser, she said: “My world has fallen apart, and my heart is broken beyond words.

“I have created this GoFundMe on behalf of my family to offer whatever help and support I can during the most devastating time of our lives.

“No parent should ever have to bury their child, especially a 17-year-old daughter and her baby.

“We are not asking for anything more than a little help towards easing the financial burden that comes with arranging the beautiful farewell that Summer and her baby deserve.



“We will give them the best send-off we possibly can, no matter what & no matter the cost.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“But if I can take even a small amount of pressure away from Mum and Dad, it would mean everything and more.”

You can donate to the GoFundme here.

News.title: Chilling moment girl, 12, runs for life after mum is 'stabbed to death' by brother
News.content:
Chilling moment girl, 12, runs for life after mum is 'stabbed to death' by brother

Police have charged a 16-year-old boy with murder after finding his mother dead in an alleged stabbing on Tuesday morning in after CCTV captured his sister, 12, running for her life

View 2 Images CCTV captured the girl running through the streets of Perth, Australia, early on Tuesday (Image: Nine)

The horrifying moment a 12-year-old girl ran for her life after her brother allegedly killed her mother has been captured on camera.

The girl was seen dashing through the streets of Perth, Western Australia (WA), early on Tuesday morning (July 21). CCTV footage from neighbours shows the child, wearing her pyjamas and dressing gown, running at speed just a minute after emergency services were called to her family home close by.

Detectives have since confirmed her mother has died in an alleged stabbing. Australian cops have charged the girl’s 16-year-old brother with murder.

Det Act Insp Jessica Securo recounted details of the incident to reporters on Tuesday: “Today, I'm here to inform the community of a tragic event that occurred in Bentley this morning.

View 2 Images Det Act Insp Jessica Securo from WA Police announces a 16-year-old boy has been arrested in connection with an alleged murder in Perth on July 21, 2026 (Image: WA Police/Facebook)

“At approximately 6:15am today, Tuesday, the 21st of July, 2026, WA police received reports of a serious incident at a residence in Mills Street in Bentley.

“Police attended the location where they located a 35-year-old female, deceased. A short time later, a 12-year-old girl was located with serious injuries at a nearby location.

“A 16 year old male, who is the son of the deceased female, and the brother of the injured girl, has been taken into police custody. I can confirm there is no ongoing risk to the wider community.”

The girl was found around 600m away from her family home, having run along the Albany Highway to flee the terror, reports the Daily Mail.

Police added she is now in hospital. Det Act Insp Securo continued: “This incident will have a significant impact on the family, friends, and loved ones of all those involved, as well as the broader community.

“Our thoughts are with them all, particularly the 12 year old girl, who remains in hospital receiving treatment. We ask that her privacy be respected during this investigation.”

On Wednesday (July 22), the 16-year-old boy appeared before Perth Children’s Court. He was charged with two crimes overnight, a WA police spokesperson said: “The 16-year-old Bentley male has been charged with 1x murder [and] 1x Attempted Unlawfully to Kill.

“He is due to appear before the Perth Children’s Court today, July 22, 2026.”

In Wednesday’s update, police added the 12-year-old girl remains in hospital. They continued: “About 6.15am Tuesday, police were called to a residence on Mills Street where they located the deceased woman.

“A short time later, a 12-year-old girl was located with serious injuries at a nearby location on Albany Highway in Cannington. She was provided emergency first aid and conveyed to hospital where she is currently receiving medical treatment and support.”

Article continues below

The investigation is ongoing and detectives urge anyone with any information relating to this incident, to contact Crime Stoppers online at www.crimestopperswa.com.au or by calling 1800 333 000. Reports can be made anonymously.

News.title: Americans dub Donald Trump 'dangerous' and 'corrupt' in scathing new survey
News.content:
Americans dub Donald Trump 'dangerous' and 'corrupt' in scathing new survey

Recent YouGov polling on America's rather colourful lexicon for its own President comes about a year and a half into Trump's second term - and things aren't going well, as per the numbers

View 3 Images Trump has been described as 'dangerous' and 'corrupt' in the new poll (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Americans are 18 months into a second presidential term of Donald Trump and they've been asked to share how they would describe the 47th President of the United States.

‌



The results, as it turns out, aren't great for the US President, with "dangerous" now the number one adjective preferred by his fellow Americans.

‌



It would seem things aren't going so well in the White House, as a range of other terms also cropped up in a recent YouGov poll. While 52% said dangerous, 49% of Americans also used “corrupt". A further 45% of them described him as a “racist”, while also calling him “out-of-touch”.

‌



There also were a number of positive words used to describe the US President, with the majority of the positive polls coming from Republican voters. Such positive terms included “honest" - used by 45% of Americans to describe Trump - and “inspiring" (40%). A further 38% described Trump as “intelligent”.

Democrats tended towards the less flattering terms, as per the data.

View 3 Images We are 18 months into Trump's term (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



The latest YouGov polling on America's rather colourful lexicon for its own President comes as Trump's approval rating continues to decline. Trump’s net approval rating in the latest poll sat at negative 24 per cent, which is lower than the same point in both his first term and the last term of his key Democratic rival Joe Biden.

His second term has been stained with a number of controversies; most notably, the sluggish release of the Epstein files, as well as his immigration crackdown which saw controversial and at-times lethal tactics used by ICE agents, and his unpopular war with Iran that has seen the cost of living skyrocket not just in America, but around the globe.

As far as the numbers go, 54 per cent of Americans disapprove of Trump’s handling of immigration, while just 39 per cent approve, according to the new poll. 54 per cent of respondents also disapproved of Trump’s handling of race relations, while 32 per cent approved.

‌



Trump, however, fared a bit better on crime. A total of 49 per cent were in disapproval, but that was in comparison to a 41 per cent approval rating, a slightly stronger figure.

Trump, however, has not lost a moment to toot that particular horn. He urged the US Senate to confirm Todd Blanche as US attorney general last week, taking to his preferred social network, Truth Social, to write: “Under Todd’s incredible leadership at DOJ, Murder is down to the LOWEST level since 1900, and we just saw the biggest one year drop in RECORDED HISTORY.”

Records do confirm Trump's claims of the biggest single year drop as homicides in major US cities have dropped sharply by over 20 per cent in 2025, following steep declines in 2023 and 2024. This does, in fact, mark the largest single-year percentage drop in recorded US history.

‌



View 3 Images Trump's popularity is dwindling (Image: Getty Images)

However, the lowest murder rate since 1900 is a murky claim as the FBI didn't standardise this sort of data until in 1960. But, that being said, if we're using the same consistent, apples-to-apples dataset, the current murder rate is definitively at its lowest point in at least 65 years. Prior to 1960, crime reporting across states and local jurisdictions was inconsistent, incomplete, and measured differently. So that claim is very difficult to verify with 100% certainty due to changes in methodology, as per crime analysts.

Fact checking Trump's murder claims aside, poor public opinion of the US President can really hinder the chances of his fellow Republicans in the November midterm elections. Historically, the party in the White House ends up losing seats in Congress halfway through the presidency, which could see a negative option gain enough momentum to have catastrophic effects.

Article continues below

CNN Chief Data Analyst Harry Enten said on Monday (July 20) that while the Democrats have an average four-point lead on a generic House ballot - as per in recent polling from The Washington Post and CNBC - this time around it is a slimmer margin than past midterm election cycles.

“Yes, they’re ahead, but they’re ahead...by only four points, which is significantly less than what we saw in 2018 and 2006, when Democrats took back the House,” he said, adding the numbers were a “warning sign". Perhaps a warning that momentum is growing... and not in favour of the US' current "dangerous" President.

News.title: UK weather maps show next 36C heatwave starts in July - 4 areas  hotter than Greece
News.content:
UK weather maps show next 36C heatwave starts in July - 4 areas hotter than Greece

The UK is set to welcome another heatwave at the end of the month with scorching temperatures of 36C triggering another heatwave, warmer than those forecast in Greece

View 3 Images Areas in the UK will climb to 36C (Image: WXCharts)

Brits are set to welcome another wave of extreme heat as temperatures are set to surpass those felt in Greece in a handful of areas.

‌



The hot spell starts at the end of July and carries on into August with the Met Office warning that conditions could turn “very warm again by the start of August”.

‌



Weather maps show temperatures climbing next week on Wednesday, July 29 as some areas are forecast a whopping 36C.

‌



View 3 Images Another heatwave is coming to the UK

This is hotter than the majority of areas in Greece, only reaching 35C, and will feel sweltering for many Brits.

Areas hotter than Greece:

Greater London

Surrey

Berkshire

Buckinghamshire

‌



View 3 Images Some areas in the UK will reach higher temperatures than the majority of Greece (Image: WXCharts)

Although not quite surpassing the Mediterranean heat, several other areas will also climb to the mid thirties.

Places near the coast in Sussex are also likely to reach 35C, as further north Hertfordshire and Cambridgeshire will also see 35C.

‌



If temperature do reach these highs it is likely chaos will erupt across the nation again, with service delays across transport and health departments.

Most areas across England are likely to sit above 30C. In Yorkshire the temperature is forecast to reach 30C, whereas in Greater Manchester the map predicts it could reach 31C.

If these temperatures continue, an official heatwave will occur.

Article continues below

A heatwave is a prolonged period of excessively hot and humid weather, lasting for three or more days typically. It is defined relative to the normal climate of a specific location, meaning a temperature that is standard in one region can be considered a heatwave in another.

The Met Office forecast for this period says: "A changeable period is likely overall, with many areas likely to see a mixture of bright or sunny spells and some rain at times.

"Temperatures will be near or above normal, warmest in the south, and perhaps becoming very warm again by the start of August."

News.title: Gran who became national hero after foiling £100k jewellery heist has died aged 85
News.content:
Gran who became national hero after foiling £100k jewellery heist has died aged 85

Ann Timson was given the nickname "Supergran" after she confronted a gang of sledgehammer-wielding thieves back in 2011 - she has now sadly passed away

View 5 Images The footage of Ann Timson, aka the supergran who took on robbers quickly went viral and propelled her to international stardom. (Image: SWNS)

A gran who became a national hero after foiling a jewellery heist by battering a group of armed robbers with her handbag has died aged 85.

‌



Ann Timson was given the nickname "Supergran" after she confronted a gang of sledgehammer-wielding thieves back in 2011. CCTV captured her charging at a gang attempting to rob £100,000 worth of watches from Michael Jones Jeweller in Northampton.

‌



The footage quickly went viral and propelled her to international stardom. She later received a Pride of Britain Award and a Queen's Commendation for Bravery from Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II.

‌



View 5 Images She ran across the street to attack a group of jewellery store robbers with her handbag (Image: SWNS.com)

Kaleb Cooper shares never seen before clips of wedding day featuring Clarkson's Farm star READ MORE :

Speaking at the time, Ann, then 71, said: "My mother's instinct kicked in and I ran across the road shouting at the lads to stop it. I was not going to stand by and watch someone take a beating so I intervened.

"As I got closer I saw it was a robbery and then I was even more angry they felt they could get away with that in broad daylight. One of the gang shot off on a scooter and nearly hit a woman and baby. I clobbered him with my shopping, but he got away. The rest were still trying to smash and grab the jewellery.

‌



"I just kept swinging my bag, then they tried to escape. I landed several blows against one lad on the back of a bike and brought him to the ground. He raised a hammer to me so I kept hitting out."

View 5 Images She passed away peacefully in her sleep after a period of declining health. (Image: SWNS)

Five men were jailed for a total of 26 years at Northampton Crown Court after admitting conspiracy to burgle in May 2011. Sentencing at the time, Judge Charles Wide QC said: "The only reason why they did not get away with even more was the extraordinary intervention by Mrs Timson.

‌



"She took on those young men who were armed with sledgehammers. No praise is too high."

Tributes have now been paid to the hero pensioner who passed away peacefully in her sleep after a period of declining health. Her son Andre Dash said her actions in tackling the thugs armed with nothing more than her handbag came as no surprise.

He said: "The first thing I thought when I saw the footage was that it was obviously my mum because of the bright red hair and bright red coat. What didn't surprise me was that she ran towards danger.

‌



"She thought a child was being attacked, which is why she ran across the road waving her handbag. It wasn't until she got there that she realised it was a jewellery robbery. What surprised me was that she wasn't seriously hurt.

"I actually found out from America. I got a phone call from a journalist in Los Angeles asking me what I thought about what my mum had done and I had absolutely no idea what he was talking about.

"I sent them a picture of mum holding my daughter Charlie when she was born because she didn't have social media. The next thing we knew she was 'Supergran'."

‌



View 5 Images Ann Timson, aka the supergran who took on robbers in Northampton with her handbag. (Image: SWNS)

Within weeks, Ann was appearing on television across the world. Andre said: "She was on the Today Show in America, appeared on television in Australia, Brazil and Germany, and we even travelled to Hamburg so she could appear on a TV programme there.

"It was extraordinary because my mum was just an ordinary Northampton lady who'd gone out shopping."

‌



Despite the passing of 15 years since the robbery, Ann remained close to staff at Michael Jones Jeweller, regularly dropping in homemade Christmas cakes and mince pies.

He said: "They were wonderful to her over the years. My mum used to take them cakes every Christmas and they've stayed in touch ever since. They'll be coming to her funeral, which means a great deal to our family."

View 5 Images Ann was born Judith Ann Brittain on January 24, 1941, at her home while her father, Charles, was serving overseas during the Second World War. (Image: SWNS)

‌



Ann spent her entire life in Northampton, growing up before raising Andre as a single mother after his father left when he was just six-months-old.

Andre said: "She was a very hard-working single mum at a time when life wasn't easy. She worked three jobs to put food on the table. She would hand-sew clothes, walk instead of taking the bus to save money and somehow always found time to bake Christmas cakes and mince pies for neighbours.

"She just worked incredibly hard, but she never complained. My mum didn't just love Northampton - she was Northampton. She travelled to America, Australia and the Bahamas, but she never wanted to live anywhere else.

Article continues below

"Northampton was home. It was where her friends were and where her heart was. She was the neighbour everybody turned to. If somebody had a problem, she'd put the kettle on, make a cup of tea and somehow make everything better.

"She was friends with everybody. She didn't have enemies. She connected people and she genuinely cared."

News.title: Daycare worker unmasked as he faces sickening 329 child abuse charges
News.content:
Daycare worker unmasked as he faces sickening 329 child abuse charges

The man faces 329 child abuse charges spanning over 16-years with police revealing over 60 childcare settings he was present at during this time in attempt to identify further victims

View 3 Images Childcare worker Hamish Tait has been charged with 329 offences over his alleged abuse of 136 children

A childcare worker in Sydney has been charged with 329 offences over his alleged abuse of 136 children at multiple daycare centres.

The alleged abuser carried out the abuse across a 16-year period, from 2009 to 2025.

Now, following his first arrest in July last year, Hamish Tait has been identified as the suspect, leaving parents 'shocked' and 'disgusted'.

View 3 Images (Image: Australian Federal Police)

Police sought a court order on Monday, July 13 and revealed his identity in an attempt to try and identify further victims.

The 35-year-old remains in custody.

His charges include 162 counts of producing child abuse material and 81 counts of filming a person engaged in a private act without consent.

Australian Federal Police said they had contacted 121 families affected by the alleged offending but are still trying to identify 22 victims.

Tait worked at or attended over 55 early years education facilities in Sydney between 2009 and 2025, but he primarily worked in the city's north-west.

The alleged abuse occurred at five facilities including four childcare centres and his own business, Wild Earthlings Glenorie.

As part of the investigation police have published a website identifying the centres where he worked to help support families.

Australian Federal Police (AFP) Acting Commander Luke Needham said: "Any form of child sexual abuse is confronting and horrific, even more so when the alleged perpetrator is an individual trusted with the care of our youth."

The force have also released imaged of distinctive clothing in an attempt to help further identify victims.

View 3 Images Investigators are trying to identify victims of alleged childcare abuser Hamish Tait Images of clothing released in bid to identify victims of alleged childcare abuser at Sydney centres https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-07-16/afp-release-images-in-sydney-childcare-abuse-investigation/106920830

The images released on Thursday, included one of a puffer vest with a dinosaur pattern, with police adding that the photo was likely taken on June 26, 2023 at a Rouse Hill childcare centre.

The release of the images is part of the "painstaking and detailed" victim identification work.

AFP Detective Acting Inspector Emmanuel Tsardoulias said officers had received over 300 calls while the operation has been ongoing.

Following the release of Tait's identity and the list of education centres, parents have been left in 'panic'.

One mother, who wished to remain anonymous told Nine news: “My first reaction was shock and disbelief but I held it together.

“We needed more information before I let panic take over.”

She said her child's daycare reassured them that Tait had only visited the centre and did not work at that branch. She added: “Our hearts just go out to those parents with kids at centres who were [allegedly] impacted by this horrific individual."

‌



Kid Fitz Learning Centres, where Tait worked, released a lengthy statement saying 'sorry for the pain that has been caused' to past parents and carers after his identity was revealed.

Mick and Melissa Scaife stated that under a non-publication order they were unable to reach out to past families before Monday.

The statement said: "The order was only discontinued in court late yesterday, meaning that we can now contact families and identify the alleged offender as Hamish Tait, who worked with us for many years and also conducted an outside business in nature play and vacation care, and consulted to other Child Care Centres.

‌



"We are shocked, saddened, disgusted, and sorry for the pain that has been caused to our extended community."

The statement continued: "Nothing is more important to us, or more fundamental to the trust you place in us, than keeping children safe while they are in our care.

"The actions of this former employee represent a profound betrayal of that trust and have left us, and our entire team, heartbroken."

Article continues below

The charges also include 22 counts of aggravated use of a child under 14 years for the production of child abuse material and 18 counts of intentionally sexually touching a child under 10 years.

Tait was linked to illegal online activity last June. Officers found child abuse material on 25 electronic devices containing 2.4million files including alleged child abuse images.

News.title: Zelensky fires Ukraine's military chief after widespread protests
News.content:
Zelensky fires Ukraine's military chief after widespread protests

General Oleksandr Syrskyi has been fired after days of protests over the removal of the popular defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov - Syrskyi has apologised if he had offended Fedorov

View 3 Images Oleksandr Syrskyi, former commander-in-chief of the Ukraine Army (Image: Andy Commins / Daily Mirror)

Ukraine's commander-in-chief General Oleksandr Syrskyi has been fired after days of protests over the removal of the popular defence minister.

‌



The country's Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov said a week ago that he had been removed from the post, amid disagreements with Syrskyi. This sparked days of street protests, magnifying a split in the military over its strategy against Russia.

‌



The following day, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky acknowledged the protests and said he was confident Fedorov would "remain on my team".

‌



View 3 Images People protest against the dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov by President Volodymyr Zelensky on July 20, 2026 in Kyiv, Ukraine (Image: Getty Images)

On Tuesday, July 21, Zelensky offered Fedorov a "prominent position in government that would allow him to unify the technical component of our state and ensure its development."

It was unclear whether Fedorov has accepted the offer.

‌



Thirty-five-year-old Fedorov is known for his approaches to technology and recruitment. His six-month tenure as defence minister coincided with Ukraine's military success and his removal from office caused major public backlash against the military chief.

View 3 Images Mykhailo Fedorov was made the new Defence Minister on January 14 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

On Monday, Zelensky met with several top generals and his chief of staff issued statements that "the position of society has been heard."

‌



Syrskyi wrote an opinion piece for local military media on Monday in which he apologised if he had offended Fedorov, claimed responsibility for establishing a drone unit as a separate military branch and rejected suggestions that he did not support the widespread use of drones, CNN reports.

Syrskyi will be replaced by Mykhailo Drapatyi, the commander of Ukraine's Joint Forces.

Drapatyi is well known for a viral 2014 video in which he drove an armoured infantry fighting vehicle through a separatist barricade in Mariupol.

Article continues below

Fedorov congratulated Drapatyi on his appointment in a post on Telegram. He said, "This is a new wind and a new hope in the struggle of free people for freedom and justice."

He also called Syrskyi and thanked him for his efforts defending Ukraine.

News.title: Pc Andrew Harper's mother slams 'slap in the face' as killers may be released early
News.content:
Pc Andrew Harper's mother slams 'slap in the face' as killers may be released early

Pc Andrew Harper was killed after he was trapped and dragged down a country road as suspects fled the scene of a burglary, now his suspects may be eligible for early release

View 6 Images Pc Andrew Harper's mum says she is 'insulted' by the early release (Image: Facebook)

Police have said they are 'disgusted' that two of Andrew Harper's killers may be eligible for early release from prison as his mother says it feels like 'a slap in the face'.

‌



Pc Harper was 28 years old when he sustained fatal injuries while responding to a quad bike theft in Sulhamstead, Berkshire, in August 2019.

‌



He died after getting caught in a strap attached to the back of a car and dragged down a country road as three teenage suspects fled the scene of the burglary.

‌



View 6 Images Debbie Adlam has been left 'insulted' by the new law and the chance her son's killers could be released early (Image: PA)

Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were passengers in the car and both 17 years old at the time, were handed 13 years in custody for manslaughter after a trial at the Old Bailey in 2020.

Now, the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) has confirmed both men may be eligible to be released from prison halfway through their sentences.

‌



Pc Harper's mother has said this feels like an "insult".

Under the new Sentencing Act, set to come into force in September, some 6,000 criminals are set to be released under the early prison release scheme.

View 6 Images (Image: PA)

‌



The Government has so far failed to rule out whether killers, rapists and paedophiles will be exempt from the scheme.

The driver of the vehicle that caused Pc Harper’s death, Henry Long, received a 16-year sentence and will not be eligible for the scheme.

Pc Harper's mother, Debbie Adlam, told the Telegraph she had received a letter from the MoJ notifying her that their sentences could be reduced.

‌



View 6 Images Henry Long, Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers (left to right) (Image: PA)

She said: “It makes me feel sick. Andrew’s life doesn’t get to come back. It feels like a slap in the face and an insult.”

She added that “people are getting a free pass for crime” in the UK.

‌



The Police Federation for England and Wales posted the update on X and labelled it “disgusting”.

Its deputy national chair, Brian Booth, said: “Police officers from across the country stood side by side to honour Andrew Harper at his funeral.

“They and every serving officer will be utterly sickened at the prospect of Bowers and Cole being back on the streets so soon”

‌



View 6 Images Debbie said "people are getting a free pass for crime" (Image: PA)

A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said: “This was a horrific crime, and our deepest sympathies are with PC Andrew Harper’s family and friends.

“In 2024, the country was facing a prison crisis and a total breakdown of law and order, with judges ordered to stop jailing dangerous criminals.

‌



“This government is committed to public safety: we are building prison places at the fastest rate since the Victorian era, and taking the difficult decisions needed to lock up the most dangerous offenders.”

It has been insisted by the Government that the act will not see early releases for offenders deemed “the most dangerous”, including those on extended determinate or life sentences.

View 6 Images Harper was due to head off on his honeymoon when he was killed (Image: Thames Valley Police/PA Wire)

‌



Pc Harper responded to the quad bike call just hours after he had been due to clock off and begin his honeymoon with wife Lissie Harper.

After her husband’s death, she campaigned for legal changes to see harsher sentences for the manslaughter of emergency workers on duty.

Harper’s Law was among the new measures in the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act.

‌



The move extends mandatory life sentences to anyone who commits the manslaughter of an emergency worker on duty including police, prison officers, firefighters and paramedics.

However, the measure is not retrospective and henceforth means Pc Harper’s killers cannot have their sentences extended.

New Justice Secretary Alex Norris has been urged to reconsider the early release scheme after being appointed by Andy Burnham on Monday.

Article continues below

Asked about reports that the Prime Minister could be working on exempting rapists and child groomers from the scheme, his spokesman said: “The Government’s fully focused on keeping the public safe.

“We’ve got no option but to take decisive action to fix the crisis in our prisons. I’m not going to get into speculation over possible policy changes.

“Of course, the Prime Minister will take decisions on all manner of policy areas in the future, including how we get justice for victims.”

News.title: Burnham pulls back on suggestion to increase income tax allowance
News.content:
Andy Burnham has pulled back from suggestions about increasing the tax-free personal allowance.

The Â£12,570 threshold has been frozen since 2021, resulting in more people being dragged into paying tax as earnings increase.

Burnham told the Times over the weekend that the "frustration about the personal allowance" he had heard while campaigning in the Makerfield by-election was "lodged in my mind".

The prime minister then told reporters on Monday that "all of this will be looked at" in the next budget but conceded any change would be expensive and "difficult given the financial circumstances in which we find ourselves".

Those close to Burnham have since told BBC News that any changes to the personal allowance are not part of his initial plan to tackle the cost of living.

It comes after Burnham told his first cabinet meeting: "We've got to show fiscal discipline. We've got to show that our commitment to the fiscal rules is real and we're prepared to make difficult decisions in relation to that."

Burnham has committed to Labour's 2024 manifesto, which included a promise not to increase the basic, higher, or additional rates of income tax.

That would rule out increasing the top rate of income tax paid by higher earners to offset the cost of lifting the personal allowance.

The Institute for Fiscal Studies has estimated that unfreezing the threshold could end up costing Â£8.5-9bn a year.

Burnham said on Monday that he was "just kind of showing I have visibility of the issue and the impact it's had."

He told reporters it would be "looked at" in the Budget, but added: "Obviously it's difficult, given the financial circumstances in which we find ourselves."

Government sources told the Telegraph on Tuesday that there were "no plans" to announce any changes to the Â£12,570 personal allowance "in the short term".

News.title: Ann Widdecombe was hit on head 21 times with hammer, prosecutors say
News.content:
Ann Widdecombe was hit on the head with a hammer 21 times at her home as she ate lunch in an attack that was caught on camera, prosecutors have told Westminster Magistrates' Court.

Prosecutor Kashif Malik said the man charged with her murder, Joshua Kerry, arrived at her house on 8 July in a red Vauxhall Corsa and entered through the front door.

Kerry, who prosecutors say was in the property for two minutes and was wearing black gloves, then allegedly hit Widdecombe repeatedly with a hammer in her kitchen, tipped her from her chair and took her wallet before driving off.

The 28-year-old from South Yorkshire later also appeared at the Old Bailey and was remanded in custody.

At the Old Bailey hearing, prosecutor Alistair Richardson said the attack on Widdecombe had been carried out with a "ferocity of violence".

Malik told the court that Widdecombe did not attend a pre-arranged online interview with Channel 5's Matt Allwright show that had been scheduled for just before 13:00 BST on 8 July.

The show's production team tried to contact Widdecombe through her personal assistant, who then asked Widdecombe's gardener to check on her, the court heard.

Prosecutors said the gardener entered the house via the open front door on 9 July and found Widdecombe lying face down on her kitchen floor with a serious head injury.

News.title: Iran war has cost US $37.5bn so far, Hegseth says, as Pentagon seeks billions more
News.content:
The war with Iran has cost the US some $37.5bn (Â£28bn) so far - an increase of nearly $8bn since the last estimate in May, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has said.

Hegseth told the Senate Appropriations Committee it was urgent that lawmakers approve another $87bn in congressional funding for the Pentagon, with $67bn of that destined for operations in the Middle East.

The hearing was disrupted several times by anti-war protesters and ended in a shouting match between the defence secretary and a senator.

It was Hegseth's first appearance on Capitol Hill since hostilities between the US and Iran restarted last week and comes after three American soldiers were confirmed killed in the region.

The White House asked Congress in April for $1.5tn for the Pentagon over the next fiscal year, which would raise American military spending to an all-time high in the modern era.

News.title: More young women in their 20s are getting type 2 diabetes
News.content:
England is seeing a "worrying increase" in young women in their 20s developing type 2 diabetes, experts at Imperial College London have warned.

The rise has largely occurred since the Covid pandemic and is closely linked to increasing obesity levels, according to an analysis of NHS data from 2011 to 2024, external.

Type 2 diabetes is serious, and can lead to severe complications, such as heart attacks and strokes.

When it develops at a younger age, the disease tends to be more aggressive, raising the risk of devastating complications and cutting lives short, according to Diabetes UK.

News.title: 'I can't afford to turn the oven on': 7.4m households struggling to buy essentials
News.content:
Elaine Yates, 77, says money worries mean she "can't remember" the last time she used her oven to cook a hot meal.

"I don't look after myself. I can't remember the last time I put the oven on. I have got an air fryer that I probably used about three weeks ago.

"I had two slices of toast yesterday and two Weetabix and fruit is all I've had to eat today."

The pensioner lives by herself in rural Northamptonshire after being widowed five years ago. Following 20 years as a full-time carer for her husband, her finances are "extremely tight", so she has felt particularly vulnerable to price rises since he passed away.

"It's really hard times, not just for me, but for thousands of others. My car costs me an arm and a leg. The fuel prices are rocketing up again, and I live in a village, so I need a car because I've got arthritis and I can't walk very far. I spend about Â£50 a week on petrol, which is more than my food bill."

Elaine often gives lifts to others in her village who don't have transport, only to find herself unable to shop alongside them.

"I've got one friend who buys clothes and I sit outside the shop because I can't afford to go in," she says. "I can't remember the last time I treated myself."

In the winter, Elaine rarely turns the heating on, and when she does she keeps the thermostat at a low 13C.

News.title: UK humanitarian worker monitored for Ebola in London hospital
News.content:
A humanitarian worker in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been medically evacuated to the UK after a potential healthcareârelated exposure to Ebola.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said the individual, who is a UK resident and has not been named, has no symptoms, and the move is purely precautionary.

The individual remains well but is being assessed and monitored at a London hospital, the statement from UKHSA said.

The hospital has not been named but the Royal Free in north London has a high level isolation unit and is the primary national centre for high consequence infectious diseases.

The incubation period of Ebola ranges from two to 21 days and the humanitarian worker will be required to isolate throughout.

The individual had been working with a humanitarian organisation supporting the Ebola outbreak response.

Ebola is a highly dangerous pathogen. Unlike flu or Covid, it is not airborne and spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids.

Symptoms come on suddenly and start like the flu or malaria, with fever, headache and tiredness. As the disease progresses, vomiting and diarrhoea develop and it can lead to organ failure. Some, but not all, patients develop internal and external bleeding.

Richard Pebody, director of epidemic and emerging infections at UKHSA, said: "The risk to the general public remains low.

"This individual has been transferred out of an abundance of caution, and we're pleased they remain well."

There are currently no confirmed cases of Ebola in the UK, the agency said.

News.title: Judge rules Trump must hand over records sought by BBC in defamation case
News.content:
A judge in Florida has ruled President Donald Trump must hand over financial records sought by the BBC as it defends itself in his $10bn (Â£7.5bn) defamation lawsuit.

The order came during the first hearing in the case, in which the US president is suing the corporation over an episode of Panorama that edited together different sections of his speech on the day of the US Capitol riot on 6 January 2021.

Judge EnjoliquÃ© Lett granted a motion by the BBC's legal team to compel the release of financial records held by the Donald J Trump Revocable Trust, which he created to manage his businesses while he is president.

The judge's ruling at Tuesday's hearing in Miami can still be appealed.

However, it amounts to a partial success in the BBC's attempt to force Trump to provide evidence for his claim of financial loss due to the Panorama edit.

The judge gave a split decision on a separate request by the BBC for documents relating to the Capitol riot itself.

News.title: Great Apes kiss and cuddle to keep the peace, says study
News.content:
Touching, embracing and kissing before stressful events may be an ancient way of building trust, according to scientists studying the behaviour of our closest ape relatives.

Researchers at Durham University studied chimpanzees and bonobos using physical contact to reassure each other ahead of conflicts over food.

One of the most surprising findings was that chimpanzees, despite their reputation for aggression, engaged in close contact, including placing fingers in one another's mouths.

"Before stressful events, they come together, they reassure each other, they touch each other, they hug each other," said Prof Zanna Clay.

News.title: Burnham tells cabinet to tackle living costs at first meeting
News.content:
Andy Burnham has promised to lead a "cost of living government," as he chaired his first cabinet meeting as prime minister.

He told his newly assembled top team that he wanted to make living expenses a key priority, and give people a "sense that help is coming" on costs.

It comes after he announced a VAT cut to household energy bills from October, in his first major announcement since taking office.

But his plan to pay for the policy by scrapping Sir Keir Starmer's digital ID scheme led to an early row over whether the plan was properly funded.

Downing Street said the estimated Â£850m cost of the VAT cut over the rest of the financial year could come from Â£1.8bn earmarked by the previous government to roll out the digital ID scheme in the next three years.

But Darren Jones, who was among a clutch of Starmer loyalists sacked from the cabinet on Monday, said the ID programme was "unfunded" and Burnham would need to set out where the money would be found.

Opposition parties also seized on the announcement, pointing out the government's budget watchdog has previously said the money to fund digital ID was due to be found from within existing budgets.

"We are only one day in and already Labour are playing fast and loose with the public finances," said Conservative shadow chancellor Sir Mel Stride.

The PM's spokesman insisted the policy would be funded by redirecting "savings" identified by departments to cover the cost of the ID scheme.

News.title: Sackings, cabinet surprises and policies: Burnham's first 24 hours as PM
News.content:
Shortly after Andy Burnham telephoned a number of Keir Starmer's allies to sack them from the cabinet on Monday afternoon, John Healey received the signal to head to Number 10.

Wearing a suit and one of his many red ties, the former defence secretary left parliament alone via a back entrance next to a pub.

"I'm on my way to a meeting," he said with a slight smile as he marched down Whitehall.

Healey's imminent appointment as chancellor was a surprise - to him, to his Labour colleagues, and to the British public.

It was a consequential moment among a flurry of announcements from the new prime minister, including today's cut in VAT on energy bills, that demonstrate the new government's intention to move at breakneck speed - at least for now.

The Conservatives support that tax cut but have questioned its funding.

Five weeks earlier Healey had weakened Keir Starmer's grip on Downing Street by quitting as defence secretary in a row over military spending.

Soon he would be back around the cabinet table alongside two others whose recent resignations had also damaged Starmer - new defence secretary Wes Streeting and new energy secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh.

Were they rewarded for rebelling and hastening Burnham's path to office? Possibly.

But all three are also widely seen as skilled operators taking on complex roles.

News.title: Scottish Labour leader Anas Sarwar set to become a minister in Burnham's government
News.content:
Scottish Labour leader Anas Sarwar is set to stand down to become a minister in Andy Burnham's government.

It would mean Sarwar leaving the Scottish Parliament and his leader role, then taking up a seat in the House of Lords.

Sarwar publicly called for Sir Keir Starmer to resign in February, provoking a political near-death experience for the then prime minister.

It is thought Sarwar, who has led the Scottish Labour Party since 2021, will become a business minister.

He was at the event in London last Friday when Burnham became the new Labour Party leader.

Scottish Labour won just 17 seats out of 129 in the Scottish Parliament elections in May.

News.title: Parts of the UK move closer to drought
News.content:
Summer so far has been exceptionally hot and dry across much of the UK, with three widespread heatwaves and the longest run of dry days in central England since 1995. England, Wales and eastern Scotland have been the driest areas over recent weeks, and this follows a very dry spring in similar regions.

England has received only 3% of its long-term average July rainfall with the south and east of England seeing no rain at all. Wisley in Surrey has seen 33 consecutive dry days.

Rainfall so far this summer has been below average across the UK as a whole, but there has been large regional contrast.

Up to the middle of summer - 15 July - parts of eastern and north-eastern England had received just 26% of their total expected summer rainfall. Areas of northern and western Scotland had more than average for the first half of the summer, though.

In Wales, where just 5% of July rainfall has fallen, Natural Resources Wales has moved the worst affected regions in the north and south-east into "prolonged dry weather status", the first step in its drought plan.

Comparisons are being made with last summer, when drought was declared across much of England, Wales and eastern Scotland. It officially ended just four months ago.

This year, drought has not developed as quickly because heavy rainfall recharged our aquifers, rivers and reservoirs during a very wet autumn and winter.

However, the UK Centre for Ecology and Hydrology says flash droughts, external with a sudden transition between wet and dry conditions are "likely to happen more often, and be more intense".

As the effects of human-induced climate change continue, the Met Office expects our summers to become hotter and drier, external in the future. In fact, by 2070, our summers could be up to 60% drier and 1-6C warmer compared to 1990.

News.title: Thames Water announces hosepipe ban for 10 million
News.content:
Thames Water has announced a hosepipe ban affecting 10.1 million customers after an "exceptionally warm and dry spring".

The restrictions mean, from Thursday, hosepipes should not be used for watering gardens or allotments, cleaning cars, filling paddling pools or swimming pools, or cleaning windows.

The water company said its region had seen 40% of average rainfall, and more days at or above 34C this year than ever recorded before.

Nevil Muncaster, director of strategic water resources, said: "We would not be taking this step unless it was necessary to protect water supplies for everyone and the environment."

The ban applies to all customers that Thames Water supplies with drinking water and comes into effect on Thursday.

The company provides water to customers across parts of Gloucestershire, Wiltshire, Surrey, the Thames Valley, Greater London, and the surrounding areas, external.

It provides water and wastewater services to 16 million customers overall.

It said water use was currently 10% above normal in the Thames Valley and Home Counties and 7% above normal in London, which amounted to an extra 100 million litres of water every day.

News.title: Russian warship carried out firing exercise off Plymouth coast
News.content:
The live-fire exercise took place in international waters and lasted for 30 minutes.

The Russian warship requested that the Royal Navy's HMS Tyne reposition to a safer distance, which it did.

The Russian frigate was also being monitored by a French military aircraft which made radio contact with the warship asking it to clarify its intentions, the BBC has been told.

BBC Verify has analysed flight and ship-tracking data which shows the position of HMS Tyne and several British military aircraft operating in and around the Channel near Plymouth on Monday.

Flight data on ADS-B Exchange indicates at least four Royal Air Force and Royal Navy aircraft were flying off the coast of Dorset mostly above the UK's territorial waters, including two Eurofighter Typhoons, a Voyager air refuelling tanker and a Super Lynx helicopter.

A French military H160M GuÃ©pard helicopter also flew out and over the Channel during the afternoon. It is not clear if this is the aircraft which made contact with the Russian warship.

Data on ship-tracking service MarineTraffic shows HMS Tyne began to broadcast its location about 40 miles off Plymouth at 13:57 BST on Monday. It remained in that location for around two hours before departing at 15:56 to return to Plymouth.

HMS Tyne has been tracking Neustrashimy since at least 16 July when both vessels were also captured in the North Sea about 36 miles miles from the port of Felixstowe in Suffolk on a satellite image.

The incident will be a reminder for the new prime minister of increased Russian naval activity near UK waters in recent months.

Last month, Royal Marine Commandos boarded a Russian "shadow fleet" oil tanker in the English Channel in a six-hour operation which was the first of its kind by UK armed forces.

Also in June, a British couple in international waters in the English Channel came across a Russian warship - Admiral Grigorovich - 23 miles off the Isle of Wight.

The frigate fired warning shots as Jane and Alan Kelvey sailed their yacht on what Russia's defence ministry said had been a "dangerous approach". However, the couple said they had not been on a "collision course".

Russian warships regularly pass through international waters in the Channel, which are separate from UK and French territorial waters.

News.title: Union plans rail strikes over train safety concerns
News.content:
A union that represents railway staff has announced plans for its members at East Midlands Railway (EMR) to take strike action over "growing safety concerns the company has failed to address".

The RMT union said it had been in dispute with EMR since April following the rollout of the 810 fleet (Aurora), which it said had been operating with a "significant number" of faults.

It said its members planned to take strike action on Saturday 1 August and the following two Saturdays.

An EMR spokesperson said any suggestion that the Hitachi Rail Class 810 fleet did not meet the required safety standards was "incorrect", and added it continued "to engage in discussions with RMT regarding this dispute".

Last week, EMR said reliability and maintenance issues with the new Aurora (Class 810) trains - made by Hitachi Rail - were to blame.

EMR has also outlined "challenges" with both the 810s and the older Class 222s, affecting the toilets, air conditioning and catering equipment.

It added the Class 222 trains had also required "additional maintenance support to accommodate increased running and operational requirements".

The operator first introduced the Aurora trains into passenger service in December, after what EMR said was a three-year delay.

News.title: Family of woman who lay dead in crash for days confronts mechanic who falsified MOT
News.content:
Angry scenes erupted outside court after the family of a woman killed in a car crash confronted a garage owner who falsified an MOT just weeks before.

Neil John Lewis, 47, pleaded guilty to fraud by false representation at Cardiff Magistrates' Court on Tuesday, and admitted he knew the car was "dangerous".

Eve Smith, 21, Darcy Ross, 21, and Rafel Jeanne, 24, died when the car given the false MOT crashed into woodland in Cardiff in March 2023. They lay undiscovered for two days. Two others survived.

As Lewis left court, the family of Ross brandished a framed photograph the dead woman, and shouted at him: "Darcy Ross, remember her name."

A decade after the release of the Hollywood musical La La Land, a great wrong has been put to rights.

In a poster for the 10th anniversary re-release of the film, Ryan Gosling’s hand has been subtly edited so that it points upward, mirroring that of his co-star, Emma Stone.

The original poster showed Gosling’s hand being held flat.

The actor previously said that he did not know the original image – shot in Griffith Park in Los Angeles – would be used to promote the film, and he held his hand that way because he thought it would look “cool”.

He dubbed the position the “La La Hand” and said that it “killed the energy” of the image.

The new hand position was unveiled on Tuesday in an Instagram post sharing the edited poster, with the caption: “A minor adjustment.”

In an earlier interview with the Wall Street Journal magazine, Gosling dubbed himself “Hamburger Hands Gosling” due to his awkward pose.

He said he had some dance experience prior to the film, but “it didn't help me at all in the end”.

In March, Gosling also reenacted the pose with his Project Hail Mary costar, Rocky the alien.

In a Facebook post shared by his partner Eva Mendes, he said: “This is my hail Mary attempt to fix my La La Hand, and my buddy Rocky’s going to help me.”

He then ran into position and struck a pose, before yelling: “How’s my hand?”

In her post, Mendes said that the La La Hand was “one of Ryan’s great regrets”, and the reenactment was an attempt to “finally make things right”.

Ryan Gosling, and his flat hand, in the original promotional material for La La Land

La La Land was directed by Damien Chazelle. It starred Gosling and Stone as a couple who meet and fall in love while pursuing their dreams in Los Angeles.

The film was a commercial success, grossing over 500 million dollars, and also received widespread critical acclaim.

La La Land was incorrectly announced as the winner of best picture at the 2017 Oscars by actor Faye Dunaway.

The cast and crew took to the stage before the correct winner, Moonlight, was announced.

Stone won best actress and Chazelle won best director at the ceremony.

La La Land will be re-released in US cinemas on 16 August and UK cinemas on 28 August.

Thailand’s prime minister Anutin Charnvirakul surprised guests in Beijing by singing “Tian Mi Mi” (Sweet Honey), a famous love song by the late Taiwanese music icon Teresa Teng, during a lunch hosted by Chinese premier Li Qiang.

The performance took place at the end of the Thai prime minister’s first official visit to China. During the trip, he also visited Shanghai, where he met Chinese president Xi Jinping.

Images from the lunch in Thai media showed Mr Charnvirakul holding a microphone at a long table as Mr Li and other officials watched and applauded, with Thai and Chinese flags displayed in the background.

The performance was the latest example of what many have described as Mr Charnvirakul’s “musical diplomacy”.

Earlier this month, during an appearance with Malaysian prime minister Anwar Ibrahim, the Thai PM played the saxophone while Mr Ibrahim sang “My Way”, the famous song associated with Frank Sinatra.

A clip of the performance went viral, with one commentator quipping that it was an episode of “ASEAN Idol”, referring to the bloc of southeast Asian nations.

During another visit to Hanoi in June, Mr Charnvirakul joined local musicians and played a traditional Vietnamese instrument in front of the country’s prime minister Le Minh Hung.

At the dinner hosted at the Vietnamese government office, musicians performed Thai songs, including “Sabai Sabai” by Bird Thongchai, using traditional Vietnamese instruments. The Thai PM joined them for at least two songs.

Mr Charnvirakul is reported to be proficient with several instruments, including the piano and the Thai flute, and is also a hobbyist pilot.

The Thai prime minister comes from a wealthy construction family but has worked to present himself as a leader with a more relatable image.

The Thai PM also performed a duet of the Thai rock song “Som San” with the teen sensation whose original name is Rattikarn “Praew” Amloy, but is better known as Nene Royal, on 14 July.

Nene gained international fame after her powerful audition on Season 21 of America’s Got Talent, where she performed The Cranberries’ “Zombie” while playing electric guitar.

According to Nation Thailand, following her viral success, the Thai government announced financial support for her continued participation in the competition. They also reportedly discussed plans to involve her as a tourism ambassador to promote Thailand’s image and “soft power” globally.

Earlier this year, Japanese prime minister Sanae Takaichi and South Korean president Lee Jae Myung surprised people after their summit in Japan by ending the meeting with a joint drum performance. The two leaders played along to K-pop hits, including BTS’s “Dynamite” and “Golden” from KPop Demon Hunters.
