World.title: AI boom lifts Mexico tech exports, complicating Trump trade goals
World.content:
Mexico City – The United States’ frenzied rush to build out AI infrastructure has boosted exports of Mexican technology, complicating President Donald Trump’s hand heading into trade negotiations.

Trump, who campaigned on boosting US manufacturing, hopes to narrow the trade deficit with Mexico during talks to update the USMCA free trade agreement, which kick off Tuesday in Mexico City.

But the dizzying rise in computer equipment exports from Mexico — the largest US trading partner — is doing the opposite.

Between January and April, Mexico tripled its sales of computer equipment to the United States compared to the same period last year, with exports topping $50 billion versus just $2.2 billion in imports, according to AFP calculations.

The sector now makes up 30 percent of all Mexican products shipped to the United States, overtaking the automotive industry as the largest component of exports.

“It’s a milestone largely driven by demand for advanced AI electronics,” Diego Flores, head of electronic and digital industries at Mexico’s Economy Ministry, told AFP.

The sector, which includes processing units and data center hardware, is not officially on the agenda for this round of negotiations.

– Explosive demand –

The most in-demand products are server racks that house AI processing cards — a key component for the data centers multiplying across the United States.

The main export hub is the Pacific state of Jalisco, dubbed the “Mexican Silicon Valley,” where an ecosystem of global industry giants and tech startups have set up shop, Flores said.

Taiwanese giant Foxconn assembles server racks in Jalisco, and serves as a strategic partner to US chip designer Nvidia.

In March, Foxconn announced $137 million in investments across two Mexican subsidiaries after estimating its production could double this year.

“The United States and Mexico will remain our primary production hubs,” Chief Executive Michael Chiang said, announcing the company would invest 30 percent more than in 2025 to expand its AI-related capacity.

Faced with booming demand, Flextronics, another tech manufacturer in Jalisco, even had to repurpose its parking lots to expand manufacturing capacity, Flores said.

Yet the boom comes amid a volatile political climate.

The Trump administration rejected a 16-year extension of the USMCA, opting instead for annual reviews with Mexico and Canada.

Washington is also continuing to push for more goods to be manufactured domestically, even as US reliance on imports from Mexico, Taiwan, and China to fuel its AI boom grows.

– ‘In the line of fire’ –

Could the thriving sector become Trump’s next tariff target?

“Nobody can say for sure,” Flores admitted. However, he expressed confidence that the sector might escape protectionist policies due to its immense strategic value to the United States.

Washington is also seeking to limit the use of Asian technology within North America, according to William Jackson, a chief emerging markets economist at Capital Economics.

“The Trump administration has to weigh the demand for these technologies and the need to stay at the forefront of AI development,” he told AFP, noting that “tariffs could prove counterproductive to that goal.”

But balancing the preservation of a booming industry with protectionist rhetoric puts the sector “very easily in the line of fire,” he warned.

That risk is heightened by the fact that Mexican manufacturers use components sourced from China and Taiwan, which Trump could view as a “backdoor” or Trojan horse for Asian technology entering the United States.

World.title: At least 41 dead in Guyana capsized ferry disaster
World.content:
Georgetown – At least 41 people died after a ferry capsized off the coast of Guyana over the weekend, the government said Tuesday.

The MV Barima was traveling from the capital Georgetown to Port Kaituma in Guyana’s inland Essequibo region when it flipped over on Saturday night.

A desperate search for survivors has been underway since early Sunday, with 77 people rescued so far and dozens more missing, according to authorities.

A government report released Tuesday revised the death toll from 27 to 41.

“A total of 41 bodies have now been recovered,” it stated.

“The first recovery for the day was made at 10:15 am (1415GMT), and 14 bodies have been retrieved as of 1 pm” Tuesday, it added.

There had earlier been confusion over how many were involved in the tragedy due to an inaccurate passenger manifest which listed 133 people aboard, Public Works Minister Juan Edghill said.

But on Tuesday, Prime Minister Mark Phillips said he was confident that 179 people had been on board when the accident occurred.

Two crew members aboard the aging ferry tested positive for marijuana after the incident, he told reporters Sunday, adding that an investigation was underway.

The ship began its journey in mid-afternoon and a distress call was received about eight hours later.

The ferry was built in 1939, according to the shipping website VesselFinder.

Boats typically travel by sea before reaching a river to arrive at Port Kaituma, which is located in the depths of a dense rainforest.

Guyana, a small English-speaking country at the northeast corner of South America, is locked in a territorial dispute with neighboring Venezuela over the oil-rich Essequibo region.

World.title: Iraqi Airways launches new digital data center for automation push
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The management of Iraqi Airways has officially opened a new digital Data Center, marking a major step forward in its comprehensive digital transformation and electronic automation project.

Ahmed Abbas, Director of the Data Center, emphasized that the project builds upon the airline’s broader automation strategy. This plan aims to implement electronic systems across all company divisions and establish an integrated digital ecosystem.

By connecting all departments, branches, and operational units under a single, unified data center, the initiative will enhance information security, unify data management, boost operational efficiency, and ensure the sustainability of digital services.

Key Strategic Objectives

Core Digital Infrastructure: Serves as one of the airline’s most critical infrastructure upgrades, modernizing IT operations to align with global standards.

Accelerated Operations: Streamlines procedures, supports integrated electronic systems, and speeds up daily operational workflows.

Enhanced Service Quality: Leverages modern technology to elevate overall service standards and customer experiences.

Government Alignment: Fulfills national e-governance mandates and Council of Ministers decisions regarding digital transformation and infrastructure development.

By launching this centralized Data Center, Iraqi Airways continues to modernize its civil aviation infrastructure, bringing faster processing, improved security, and higher-quality digital services to both internal operations and passengers.

World.title: Trump ‘not finished’ with Iran as Tehran steps up strikes
World.content:
Tehran – President Donald Trump said Tuesday that the United States was not finished attacking Iran, as Tehran stepped up its strikes across the Middle East.

The US leader projected that it would take the Islamic republic more than 20 years to rebuild from damage sustained in the Middle East war, two weeks after fighting between the decades-old foes resumed.

“If we left right now, it would take Iran 20, 25 years to rebuild,” he said. “We’re not finished at all… we’re not leaving right now.”

His comments came after Jordan, Kuwait and Bahrain came under attack Tuesday.

Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels meanwhile said they would blockade Saudi Arabia’s ports, threatening to throw energy markets into chaos after Iran’s Strait of Hormuz blockade.

Bahrain said it intercepted Iranian attacks as sirens sounded multiple times in the kingdom, with Kuwait and Jordan also announcing they had intercepted drone and missile strikes.

Kuwait has said that Tehran hit multiple power and water desalination plants across the country over the past days, including on Monday, forcing residents to ration energy consumption.

Iran’s Guards confirmed a strike on Jordan, claiming they had targeted a “complex housing US terrorist forces in the region of Rukban”.

The Iranian army had earlier said it targeted US assets in Kuwait and Bahrain, including air defence systems, radar installations and administrative buildings.

“With this radar sweep, the enemy should prepare for even more decisive and powerful waves of drone and missile attacks,” the Guards said in a statement carried by state news agency IRNA.

– Houthi threat –

US President Donald Trump said he would “take care of” the Houthi rebels if the Iran-backed militant group followed through on its threatened blockade of Saudi ports.

“If something like that happens, we take care of it,” Trump said. “You know, we’ve done that with the Houthis before, and we haven’t heard from them in a while since we did what we did originally.”

Saudi Arabia strongly condemned the threat from what it called the “terrorist Houthi militia” and said it “continues to support the brotherly Yemeni people and their legitimate government”.

It remains unclear how the Houthis would implement their blockade of Saudi ports, and oil markets eased slightly despite the threat from Iran’s ally against the world’s biggest crude exporter.

But maritime intelligence provider Vanguard Tech said a Singapore-flagged tanker and a Liberia-flagged tanker both “reversed course” in the Red Sea after loading crude at the Saudi port of Yanbu following the Houthi warning.

Should the Houthis make good on their threat to blockade Saudi ports, that would put at risk Riyadh’s ability to bypass Hormuz for some of its oil exports and have major repercussions for the global economy.

Saudi Arabia and the Houthis traded fire last week for the first time in years, threatening a 2022 truce in their years-long conflict, but the rebels have largely remained on the sidelines since Israel and the US attacked Iran in late February.

The Revolutionary Guards said on Tuesday that two tankers attempting to transit Hormuz “were hit by explosions, resulting in massive fires that brought them to a standstill”.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) earlier reported that an “unknown projectile” struck a tanker off the coast of Oman.

– ‘Still struggling’ –

Following the deaths of at least three US soldiers in recent days, the US launched a new round of attacks against Iran on Monday it said was “designed to further degrade Iranian military capabilities used to attack commercial shipping” in the Strait of Hormuz.

The deaths bring to 17 the number of fatalities among US service members. Nearly 100 US service members have been wounded since war resumed on July 7, the Pentagon said Monday.

Shahin, a 34-year-old embroiderer from Iranshahr in southeast Iran, said: “We’re still struggling to secure our most basic life necessities, and now we’re dealing with destruction from the war on top of it.”

As Iran stepped up its attacks in the Gulf, Kuwait’s foreign ministry on Tuesday said it had summoned Iran’s ambassador over a strike against a ship passing through the Hormuz strait the day before.

Despite the latest fighting, Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said diplomatic exchanges with Washington via mediators were ongoing.

Mediator Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called for restraint from all warring sides during a meeting with Iran’s Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni on Tuesday.

Sharif urged the sides to “refrain from actions that could further destabilise the region”, his office said.

World.title: E-payment firms to assist CBI in driving Iraq’s digital transition
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Governor of the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) Nizar Hussein met on Tuesday with representatives of licensed electronic payment companies to enhance their role in supporting the country’s digital transformation.

The meeting addressed the role of e-payment firms in carrying out the CBI’s strategy to develop the electronic payments system and enhance financial inclusion.

Hussein noted that in the next term, electronic payment firms must improve the services provided to customers while adhering to the highest quality standards.

The step will boost public trust in electronic payment systems, foster the development of new digital payment solutions, reduce dependency on cash, and develop the digital economy, according to a statement released by the CBI.

Hussein urged electronic payment firms to adhere to international standards governing international financial transactions to open up more chances for sector development, boost card limitations, and introduce new financial services that match residents’ requirements.

The meeting addressed procedures that the CBI would adopt with electronic payment firms to eliminate card misuse, improve the security of the payment system, boost operational limitations, and offer advanced services to residents.

Hussein also called for increasing collaborations with CBI-licensed banks to achieve financial sector integration and develop a modern, secure, and innovative payment system.

World.title: Indian Oil Corp stops loading Iraqi oil amid Hormuz instability
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Sources told Reuters that Indian Oil Corp. (IOC) has stopped loading Iraqi oil from Basrah Oil Terminal due to increasing risk and assaults on vessels crossing the Strait of Hormuz.

Around July 23, the state-run IOC planned to transport 2 million barrels of Iraqi oil via the mega-sized crude carrier Lila Jamnagar.

Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd, a different state refiner, has also halted plans to transport oil from Iraq via the Indian-flagged Aframax tanker Desh Gaurav.

Following the resumption of military operations in the Strait of Hormuz, India has advised shipping companies to refrain from assigning Indian seafarers to vessels operating in that region.

Ship captains were also advised to be cautious regarding security in the Arabian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, and surrounding waterways and to continuously check navigational warnings.

Prior to the war, the Strait of Hormuz between Iran and Oman served as the primary transit route for around a fifth of the world’s oil and gas supplies.

Tensions have escalated since the truce between Washington and Tehran was broken in early July. This breakdown has resulted in attacks that have disrupted trade through the crucial waterway.

World.title: Turkish Transport Minister arrives in baghdad to elevate transport ties and Development Road cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Turkish Minister of Transport and Infrastructure Abdulkadir Uraloğlu arrived in Baghdad on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, to conduct high-level talks with Iraqi officials aimed at taking bilateral cooperation in transport, logistics, and telecommunications to a higher level.

Minister Uraloğlu was officially welcomed at Baghdad International Airport by Deputy Minister of Transport Hazem Razi Lafta, before holding bilateral talks with Iraqi Minister of Transport Wahb Al-Hasani at the state guesthouse in Baghdad.

Strategic Focus: The Development Road Project Primary Agenda: Fast-tracking execution phases of the multi-billion-dollar Development Road project, an international rail and highway network linking Grand Faw Port in southern Iraq directly to Turkey and European commercial markets.

Diplomatic Context: The visit serves as a key logistical precursor ahead of Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi’s upcoming official state visit to Turkey scheduled for July 28, 2026.

The visit underscores the massive economic weight and trade synergy between the two neighboring nations:

Heavy Commercial Volume: Bilateral trade volume between Iraq and Turkey stands at approximately $15 billion to $17 billion annually, with joint diplomatic initiatives aiming to expand total trade to $24 billion.

Key Trading Partner: Iraq consistently ranks among Turkey’s top export destinations globally (exceeding $12 billion in Turkish exports alone), primarily spanning food products, construction materials, machinery, and consumer goods.

Infrastructure Footprint: Turkish construction firms have historically undertaken over 1,100 development projects in Iraq valued at more than $36 billion, making Iraq one of the largest markets for Turkish engineering and infrastructure expertise worldwide.

By coordinating transport routes and cross-border digital networks through the Development Road project, both Baghdad and Ankara aim to secure long-term transit revenue, streamline regional supply chains, and further integrate their high-volume trade partnership.

World.title: National Security Service foils clandestine drone manufacturing cell in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s National Security Service (NSS) announced on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, the successful disruption of a clandestine operation attempting to manufacture unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) inside the capital city of Baghdad.

Executed under the direct supervision of the Judge of the Third Investigative Court, the intelligence-led raid resulted in the arrest of three primary suspects and the seizure of a makeshift production facility.

In an official statement and accompanied by video documentation of the tactical operation, the NSS confirmed that its specialized intelligence units executed judicial arrest and search warrants following precise surveillance.

The security sweep uncovered an active workshop equipped with 25 prefabricated drone airframes, along with specialized carbon fiber sheets, custom molds, and technical assembly tools utilized in the production and fabrication of long-range drones.

Seizure Inventory & Intelligence Breakdown

Arrests: 3 primary suspects apprehended under judicial warrants issued by the Third Investigative Court.

Drone Airframes: 25 completed and semi-completed UAV structural fuselages.

Manufacturing Materials: Industrial-grade carbon fiber panels, custom molds, and precision technical tooling.

Status: Disrupted prior to final assembly and operational deployment.

Ongoing Probe: Investigations are actively expanding to determine potential linkages between the illicit workshop, regional factional networks, or broader national security threats.

The NSS emphasized that the covert operation was completely dismantled before the manufactured drones could reach operational completion or be integrated into regional flight networks.

Legal proceedings have been initiated, and the suspects remain in federal custody as investigators work to identify supply chains and potential organizational ties before referring the perpetrators to the judiciary.

World.title: NEET protest: TVK slams govt; Rahul, Priyanka released from detention — top developments
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were released after being detained by Delhi Police during a protest near Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence.

The party had marched to Lok Kalyan Marg demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged paper leak and the police action against student protesters.

The protests also drew support from several opposition leaders, while Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) strongly criticised the Centre over Rahul Gandhi's detention and renewed its demand for the abolition of NEET.

Meanwhile, the BJP accused the Congress of politicising the issue and defended the police action, saying the protest near the Prime Minister's residence was held without permission.

The developments came as thousands of protesters returned to Jantar Mantar to continue the agitation.

TVK condemns Rahul's detention, seeks NEET abolition



Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) condemned the detention of Rahul Gandhi and criticised the police action against opposition leaders.





"The crushing of democracy in the capital is strongly condemnable! The arrest of Lok Sabha Opposition Leader Mr. Rahul Gandhi, who joined the field in support of the youth's non-violent protest held in Delhi, by being dragged by the Delhi Police and carried away in handcuffs, is a blatant attack on democratic rights. This is strongly condemnable," the party said.

TVK also renewed its opposition to the NEET examination.

"From the moment the NEET exam was implemented, not only has its credibility been lacking, but students continue to face mental stress, with their future dreams turning into a massive question mark. The harm caused to students every year due to the NEET exam shows no sign of stopping. Therefore, we strongly demand that the Union government completely abolish the NEET exam," it said.

Rahul, Priyanka released after detention



Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and several opposition leaders were detained after Congress workers marched towards the Prime Minister's residence at Lok Kalyan Marg.

Rahul Gandhi, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and other leaders were taken to Chhatrasal Stadium before being released later in the day. Priyanka Gandhi was taken to Mandir Marg Police Station, where Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi later arrived.

Congress leaders said they protested because they were not allowed to raise the NEET issue in Parliament. Rahul Gandhi said they marched to the Prime Minister's residence "to demand answers from him for the brutalities against young students yesterday" and demanded the resignation of the Prime Minister and the Home Minister.

The protest was joined by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, KC Venugopal, Pawan Khera, Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar, Kerala Leader of Opposition VD Satheesan, Supriya Sule and several other opposition leaders.

Pradhan hits out at Congress



Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan accused the Congress of using students for political purposes.

"LoP Shri @RahulGandhi and @INCIndia continue to shamelessly exploit students as political tools to manufacture disruption during the Monsoon Session of Parliament," he wrote on X.

He said the government was ready for a discussion on NEET in Parliament but alleged that the Congress preferred "political spectacle over democratic debate".

"We owe our students more than outrage. We owe them answers, reforms and accountability. That is exactly what our government remains committed to delivering," Pradhan said.

BJP MP Sambit Patra also criticised the protest, saying demonstrations should be held only at designated locations.

He said the Prime Minister's residence is a high-security zone and staging a protest there without permission was "inappropriate".

Police detail injuries, register six FIRs



Delhi Police said six FIRs have been registered in connection with the violence during Monday's Parliament march. Two FIRs were registered at Parliament Street police station, while one each was registered at Connaught Place, Tilak Marg, Barakhamba Road and Kartavya Path police stations.

DCP Northeast Delhi Rahul Alawal said six police personnel were injured during the violence. He said Constable Mohit suffered serious injuries to his head, below his eyes and on his legs and remains on medical rest. Additional DCP Sandeep Lamba, Inspector Rampal Goswami and some other officers have resumed duty despite being advised to rest.

Station House Officer of Connaught Place police station Sukhbir Singh Malik said he was assaulted when a section of protesters allegedly turned violent near Regal Cinema.

Malik said his helmet prevented a head injury, but he suffered injuries to his elbows, calf muscle and waist after being dragged to the ground. The police said several other personnel, including an ACP, an Inspector, a Head Constable and a driver, were also injured.

Sonam Wangchuk continues fast



Activist Sonam Wangchuk continued his indefinite hunger strike after being shifted from Safdarjung Hospital to Medanta Hospital in Gurugram following directions from the Delhi High Court.

Sources told news agency ANI said Union Health Minister JP Nadda and Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office Jitendra Singh visited Medanta Hospital to enquire about Wangchuk's health.

The Delhi High Court directed Medanta Hospital to form a specialised medical team to supervise Wangchuk's treatment while allowing him to continue his fast under constant medical supervision. His wife, Gitanjali Angmo, said he would continue the hunger strike in solidarity with students allegedly injured during the police action.

World.title: 'Nadir of Indians' integrity': Allahabad HC judge slams Ram Mandir theft, backs death penalty
World.content:
Allahabad High Court on Ram Temple theft (ANI image on right)

Backs death penalty

Supreme Court orders fresh SIT probe

The case so far

NEW DELHI: Allahabad High Court judge, on Tuesday, made strong observations on the alleged embezzlement of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya, saying the incident reflected the"nadir of Indians' integrity"and that those unfazed by it could not be shamed.The observations were made while the bench was hearing a matter related to the Uttar Pradesh government's recent bulldozer actions. During the hearing, Justice Sreedharan criticised the deep-rooted corruption in public institutions.The judge also advocated the death penalty for offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act.Justice Atul Sreedharan said, "The recent controversy relating to the theft of donations at the Ram temple is the proverbial last straw on the camel's back. Nothing can shame people who remain unfazed by the theft at the Ram temple which epitomises the nadir of Indians' integrity".""The average Indian has accepted corruption as normal. He does not consider it wrong unless someone is caught. India ranks 91st out of 182 countries on the Transparency list, and even that does not make us feel ashamed," he added.The Supreme Court earlier has directed the constitution of a fresh Special Investigation Team (SIT) to probe the alleged Ram Mandir donation theft case.A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said the new SIT should be led by a senior IPS officer to ensure a fair and conclusive investigation."We only want to issue a word of caution. Do not politicise this matter. At first glance, this appears to be an offence under criminal law. It must be investigated fairly, independently and with complete honesty. The investigation should be taken to its logical conclusion," the CJI observed.The controversy erupted on June 7 after former Samajwadi Party minister Pawan Pandey alleged that donations worth Rs 5 crore to Rs 7.5 crore had been stolen from the Ram Mandir.Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav questioned the government's silence and sought a judicial probe, while Ram Mandir Trust general secretary Champat Rai rejected the allegations. BJP leader Dr Rajneesh Singh later demanded a CBI investigation, following which the Prime Minister's Office sought a report from the temple trust.An FIR was registered on June 25 on the complaint of trustee Krishna Mohan. Police has subsequently arrested eight accused in the matter till now.

World.title: 4 out of 10 healthcare workers worldwide face violence: WHO
World.content:
The incident took place at the Shastri Nagar Hospital, run by the Kalyan Dombivli Municipal Corporation (KDMC), in Kalyan on Monday evening.

MUMBAI: As the medical fraternity continues to press for stronger legal protection following Shiv Sena corporator Ramesh Mhatre's assault on doctors at Dombivli's Shastri Nagar Municipal Hospital, Indian Medical Association (IMA) Tuesday shared an interactive digital grid documenting 100 assaults on doctors reported from across the country in recent years.The campaign comes even as studies show that violence against healthcare workers by patients or their relatives has emerged as a global public health concern. A review published in the indexed medical journal, Atencion Primaria, found that doctors in both developed and developing countries face workplace violence. It reported lifetime prevalence rates of 91% in Germany, 90% in China, 84.5% in Peru, 84% in Turkey and 77.3% in India.According to WHO, four in 10 healthcare workers experience physical violence during their careers. When verbal abuse is included, the proportion rises to over 60%.The triggers for the attacks are universal, be it Mumbai or Singapore: overcrowded hospitals, staff shortages, long waiting times, poor communication and unrealistic patient expectations.Dr Santosh Kadam, former state IMA chief blames the attacks on impatience."We are becoming an impatient society. Everyone wants speedy results. People are spending money, so they want a 100% result," he said.Experts caution that ha-rsher laws alone are unlikely to solve the problem. They underline the need for a combination of measures, including greater investment in healthcare, stronger enforcement of laws, improved doctor-patient communication and awareness campaigns. Many Euro-pean countries observe Ma-rch 12 as a day to raise awareness about violence against healthcare professionals.In India, 19 states have enacted laws to protect healthcare workers, attacks continue. "What we need is one national law,'' said Dr Suhas Pingle, former Maharashtra Medical Council member.In Maharashtra, 738 cases were registered under Maharashtra Medicare Service Persons and Medicare Service Institutions (Prevention of Violence and Damage or Loss to Property) Act between 2010 and 2021, but only four ended in convictions.Spain strengthened legal protection by recognising assaults on healthcare workers as crimes against the state; assaults dropped by half. In Singapore, those who abuse healthcare workers can face a fine of up to S$5,000, jail for up to 12 months, or both.In India, Dr Kadam said, abuse is far more widespread than official records indicate. Dr Pingle said, "Medical practice has become tech-driven and expectations of patients are sky high. Barely 2% of the budget is meant for healthcare. Doctors have to see hundreds of patients in a short span of time. This creates an environment where the risk of violence is high," he said.

World.title: SC seeks Maharashtra zila parishads poll schedule by Friday
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

Tuesday sought Maharashtra State Election Commissionâs response by Friday on issuance of a notification to conduct polls in Aug-Sept for remaining 20 zila parishads and 211 nagar panchayats and brushed aside SECâs ongoing SIR exercise as the reason for the delay in holding polls.

Senior advocate Balbir Singh, appearing for SEC, told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and Vipul M Pancholi that most of state govt officers, who are likely to be engaged in the election work related to zila parishads and nagar panchayats, are at present engaged in carrying out the SIR of poll rolls in the state.

When the SEC said it intended to conduct these elections in Feb-March next year after the completion of SIR work, the bench said SIR is conducted by EC and not SEC.

âWe will ensure you get adequate manpower,â it said.

The bench asked the SEC to come out with an election schedule by Friday.

The batch of matters before the bench raised myriad yet sensitive issues. One challenged the transposition of socially and economically backward classes (SEBC), identified for reservation in govt employment and admission to govt schools and colleges, with reserving constituencies in elections. It said OBCs are politically advanced and powerful in most of the states and a five-judge SC bench in its 2010 judgement in Krishna Murthy case had mandated that constituencies should be reserved for politically backward sections.

World.title: 50% quota for ex-Agniveers in CAPF, Assam Rifles posts: MHA
World.content:
CRPF introduced a similar amendment in recruitment rules last year

NEW DELHI: Former Agniveers will get 50% reservation in posts of constable (general duty) and rifleman in the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and Assam Rifles, the home ministry told Lok Sabha on Tuesday.In reply to a written question, junior home minister Nityanand Rai said govt has created a new category of 'ex-Agniveer' in the aforementioned posts with the provision of 50% vacancies, a three-year relaxation in the prescribed upper age limit and an age relaxation of five years beyond the prescribed age limit for candidates from the first batch of ex-Agniveers.Apart from this, he added, ex-Agniveers applying to CAPF constable (general duty) and rifleman posts will be exempted from the physical standards test, physical efficiency test and written examination. "A dedicated ex-Agniveer wing under the ministry of home affairs has been established for the purpose of coordinating further progression of ex-Agniveers," said Rai.The first batch of Agniveers have not yet completed their four-year tenure. A notification issued by home ministry in Dec 2025 had amended the Border Security Force, General Duty Cadre (Non-Gazetted) Recruitment Rules, 2015, to increase the quota for ex-Agniveers in constable (general duty) posts to 50% from 10%."By direct recruitment (including 50%), vacancies shall be reserved for ex-Agniveers in every recruitment year, 10% for ex-servicemen and up to 3% for combatised constable (tradesmen) in absorption of annual vacancy," the notification had stated. The CRPF introduced a similar amendment in recruitment rules in May last year.

World.title: Students protest: From Ladakh to London, Mumbai to Hyderbad, stir spreads
World.content:
Ladakh stepped out. London rallied. Indore mobilised. Dehradun marched. Hyderabad joined. Mumbai dug in. Protesters rallied across geographies Tuesday, drawing students behind activist Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike for education reforms.

For the first time since Wangchuk began his fast in solidarity with Cockroach Janta Party's agitation, scores of students marched through Kargil carrying banners reading "Save merit, Save students, Save the Nation" and "We Stand With Sonam Wangchuk", while a candlelit march lit up Leh's main market.

Arif Ali, president of Ladakh Students Union of Kargil, called the protest peaceful and democratic.

The slogans travelled. Solidarity protests reached UK, where demonstrations were held in Edinburgh, Glasgow, Manchester, and outside Indian high commission in London.

Organised by SFI-UK, the rallies drew thousands of Indian students and left-wing groups, who demanded "accountable, fair and transparent education" and backed students' right to protest peacefully.

Around 900 people, mostly students aged 20 to 24, have been charged in eight FIRs filed in Mumbai in connection with CJP's protests over the past three days. Protesters said they received police notices on WhatsApp Tuesday.





The demonstrations, which gained momentum over the weekend, continued with placards and slogans.

In Indore, over 1,000 students, joined by teachers, parents and citizens, gathered near Tantya Bhil statue in support of protesters in Delhi. "What started with just a handful of students has now become a movement for every aspirant who wants a fair exam system," Sakshi Baheria said after bringing food for protesters.

Hundreds took to the streets in Dehradun, marching and demanding Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and early resolution of pending recruitment exams and results in Uttarakhand. Police stopped them near Secretariat, leading to clashes.

Police detained nine protesters in Vadodara for demonstrating without permission. In Hyderabad, police detained several protesters linked to All India Students Federation during a march against police action on CJP supporters in Delhi.

(Inputs from Dehradun, Indore, Mumbai & agencies)

World.title: India hosts maiden Op Southern Readiness in Kochi, 26 nations join maritime exercise
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A four-day multinational maritime security training engagement, Operation Southern Readiness 26-2, commenced at the Southern Naval Command in Kochi on Monday. Hosted by the

âs Southern Naval Command, the engagement is being conducted under the aegis of the Navy-led Combined Task Force 154 (CTF 154), in partnership with Combined Maritime Forces (CMF), and has brought together 254 participants from 26 countries, supported by 74 facilitators and four international organisations, and Subject Matter Experts.

The exercise marks the maiden conduct of Operation Southern Readiness in India and represents an important milestone in the growing engagement between the Indian Navy and CMF.

CTF 154, CMF's dedicated Training Task Force, is currently commanded by the Indian Navy and is focused on strengthening capacity, interoperability and professional readiness of CMF partner nations through multinational maritime training.

The opening day, broadly themed around the subject of ship management and special training, combined professional interaction with subject matter experts and practical exposure. A session by the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) addressed maritime security threats in the Red Sea and Western Indian Ocean.

Over the next three days, participants will continue with a diverse programme of professional sessions, simulator-based training and practical activities covering key aspects of contemporary maritime security. The engagement reflects the Indian Navy-CMF partnership in advancing regional capacity building, interoperability, and collective maritime security while promoting professional exchange and stronger relationships among participating nations.

Conduct of Operation Southern Readiness by the Southern Naval Command further augments the role of the Indian Navy as the preferred security and training partner in the region.

World.title: India summons Russian envoy, protests hit that killed 4 Indians on ship
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India summoned Russian charge d'affaires, Vladimir Ladanov, to protest the attack on a commercial vessel in Ukraine that left four Indian seafarers dead. The ministry of external affairs (MEA) said in a statement that it conveyed India's grave concerns and unequivocal condemnation of the attack on commercial vessel MV Golden Leo, emphasising that such attacks undermine the safety, security, and stability of international maritime commerce.

The Russian diplomat was requested to convey India's concerns to his authorities that the targeting of commercial shipping and the resulting loss of civilian lives are unacceptable and must be avoided, according to the ministry.

The Guinea-Bissau-flagged vessel, carrying crew members from Syria and India, was hit by Russian cruise missiles while leaving the port of Odesa in Ukraine. This is the first time that Indian seafarers have been killed in the Russia-Ukraine conflict.

Kremlin spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, told reporters that Moscow was in touch with India on the matter. "We are explaining our position. Most importantly, our armed forces are striking - and will continue to strike - vessels involved in transporting ammunition, weapons, and so on for the purposes of the Kyiv regime," he said.

The vessel had 17 crew members, including five Indian nationals, according to the MEA.

World.title: Jantar Mantar protest LIVE: Hundreds order food for protesters; Wangchuk shifted to Medanta Hospital in Gurugram
World.content:
LoP in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi and several opposition leaders, including NCP (SP) president Sharad Pawar and AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal, visited the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) protest site at Jantar Mantar on Tuesday (July 21, 2026), a day after the police crackdown on its ‘Sansad Chalo’ march, and extended support to the agitation over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations.

Also read: Police file four FIRs amid flak over crackdown on protesters

The Delhi police on Tuesday registered four FIRs against unknown individuals for rioting, assault on public servants, damage to public property and other offences during Monday’s (July 20, 2026) Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest.

Hundreds of people across the country and abroad ordered food with the location as the Jantar Mantar protest site and instructions to give the food to the protestors. The food items ranged from pizzas, burgers, momos, to thaalis.

Also read: The salt of democracy

Meanwhile, activist Sonam Wangchuk was discharged from the Safdarjung Hospital on Tuesday (July 21, 2026) evening and shifted to Medanta Hospital in Gurugram for further treatment in compliance with a Delhi High Court order.

World.title: Trump approves nuclear agreement that may allow Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium
World.content:
President Donald Trump has approved an agreement with Saudi Arabia that could potentially provide the kingdom with uranium enrichment capability for its civilian nuclear program, according to two people familiar with the matter.

The people, who were not authorised to comment publicly about the yet to be formally announced decision, said the agreement is expected to be announced publicly as early as Wednesday (July 22, 2026).

The deal is expected to last 30 years and is also expected to involve U.S. firms in developing the programme. The deal could allow for the building of a uranium enrichment facility in Saudi Arabia following a joint U.S.-Saudi study.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the decision, which was first reported on by the Wall Street Journal.

World.title: Namma Karnataka Sene chief Basawaraj arrested for assault on GBA officials during footpath clearance drive; total arrests rises to 11
World.content:
The Commercial Street police in Bengaluru have arrested Basawaraj Padukote, the State president of Namma Karnataka Sene, in connection with the assault on government officials during an anti-encroachment drive under the Safe Footpath Campaign in Shivajinagar.

Mr. Padukote, whom the police identified as the main accused, is the 11th person arrested in the case. The police on a Tuesday (July 21, 2026) had arrested 10 people.

According to Bengaluru Police, he allegedly led the attack on officials who were carrying out an encroachment removal drive. The police also said Mr. Padukote has a criminal background.

The latest arrest comes after the Employees’ Association of the Greater Bengaluru Authority threatened to launch a pen-down strike if those responsible for the attack were not arrested. The association had also demanded adequate police protection for civic staff engaged in the ongoing anti-encroachment operations.

Police said the investigation is continuing and further action will be taken based on the mobile phones recording and CCTV evidence collected.

On Tuesday, high drama had erupted near the Shivajinagar Bus Stand in Central Bengaluru when officials of the GBA began a footpath clearance drive, with a group of people launching an attack on the officers, assaulting them with chairs and helmets, and using pepper spray to chase them away. Five people were injured in the incident, including Assistant Executive Engineer Madhav Rao .

World.title: Rahul changed goalposts to end sit-in, says govt.; BJP terms protest at PM’s residence a ‘symbol of anarchy’
World.content:
The Union government and the BJP accused Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha of “changing the goalposts” with his demands for ending his sit-in outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s official residence over the NEET paper leak, resulting in Opposition leaders being summarily detained by Delhi Police, with BJP’s national president Nitin Nabin terming his conduct “a symbol of anarchy”.

The man at the centre of the controversy, Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan also spoke up late on Tuesday evening (July 21, 2026), posting on X that Mr. Gandhi was “shamelessly” exploiting students as a “political tool”.

“LoP Shri @RahulGandhi and @INCIndia continue to shamelessly exploit students as political tools to manufacture disruption during the Monsoon Session of Parliament,” he posted, adding that Mr. Gandhi chose to stage a sit-in outside Prime Minister Modi’s residence disregarding security protocols.

Students deserve better, says Pradhan

“Even after the government conveyed its readiness for a comprehensive discussion, the Congress chose political spectacle over democratic debate,” Mr. Pradhan said. “For Rahul Gandhi, this is not about students. This is about manufacturing confrontation after every genuine avenue for discussion has been opened. The students of India deserve far better than being treated as props in a political campaign. They deserve certainty over chaos, solutions over slogans and responsibility over disruption. We owe our students more than outrage. We owe them answers, reforms and accountability. That is exactly what our government remains committed to delivering,” Mr. Pradhan added.

LoP Shri @RahulGandhi and @INCIndia continue to shamelessly exploit students as political tools to manufacture disruption during the Monsoon Session of Parliament.



Shri @RahulGandhi and @INCIndia chose to stage a dharna outside the Hon'ble Prime Minister's residence , causing… — Dharmendra Pradhan (@dpradhanbjp) July 21, 2026

Union Minister of State for the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) Jitendra Singh, the designated interlocutor on behalf of the government to speak to Mr. Gandhi, said the government was willing to discuss the NEET paper leak issue and the behaviour of the administration with regard to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protest march held on Monday (July 20, 2026), but Mr. Gandhi demurred having agreed earlier.

“When we went there [the dharna spot in front of Mr. Modi’s official residence] and very politely, very humbly I tried to plead before Rahul Gandhi that this was not the manner in which he should be indulging. He said yes, he was ready to suspend this dharna provided he was given an assurance that government was ready for a discussion in Parliament on the issue of NEET exam, the paper leakage, [and] all those issues related to this,” said Mr. Singh.

Subsequently, the Minister said he got in touch with the top leadership of the government and was asked to convey that they were willing to concede the demand.

When he returned to Mr. Gandhi, the Leader of Opposition brought up an additional demand for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

‘Not gentlemanly’

“Then, I politely tried to submit before him. I said look here, this is not done. Now, this is not a gentlemanly behaviour. He said no, it’s my wish, my demands have changed. I said this doesn’t behove an LoP to change stance and change goalposts that frequently. So, we had no option but to leave this part,” he said.

Following this, Mr. Singh left the area and Mr. Gandhi, Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Akhilesh Yadav, Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and others were detained by the Delhi Police, after an unseemly scuffle.

BJP’s national president Nitin Nabin raised objections to Mr Gandhi undertaking his sit-in at Prime Minister Modi’s residence, terming the move as a “symbol of anarchy”. “We have consistently maintained that Rahul Gandhi is emerging as a symbol of anarchy. Certain parliamentary offices do not belong to any single party; the Prime Minister is not merely the leader of one party but the elected representative of 1.4 billion citizens. The behaviour exhibited by Rahul Gandhi and his team and their attempt to incite anarchy during their visit to the Prime Minister’s residence today clearly indicates that this is not the politics of dissent, but rather the politics of anarchy,” said Mr Nabin in a statement.

He pointed out that he saw Tueday’s incident as “a dark day in India’s political history”, adding that the BJP had also served in the Opposition for long period without “breaching such boundaries.”.

“When Rahul Gandhi set conditions, they were accepted. Yet, it is unfortunate that a person holding the office of LoP backs out once the process moves forward... I would tell our colleagues in the Congress opposition that we are always ready for any kind of dialogue on the floor of Parliament,” he added.

According to senior government sources, the venue of Mr Gandhi’s sit-in location being right outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s official residence was the reason for the quick reaction and engagement demonstrated by the government. “It is not a designated place of protest and is a high-security zone,” said one senior Minister.

AAP MP Sanjay Singh posted on X that the government was shaken by the strength of the protests spearheaded by CJP (which has the backing of AAP) and the BJP wanted to counter this leading to the sit-in by Mr. Gandhi. “To weaken the CJP’s dharna, Modiji has seated Rahul Gandhi on a dharna at his residence,” Mr. Singh posted. This led to angry reactions from the Congress, and an opportunity for the BJP to say that the protests were more about who gets the credit of raising the issues faced by students and not the students themselves.

National in-charge of BJP’s Information & Technology department Amit Malviya posted on X: “It is quite obvious that the sponsored protests were never about students. No affected student was given a platform. Opposition politicians frequented Jantar Mantar in search of political relevance, and now we see Congress and AAP squabbling over credit.” He claimed that “no one other than the BJP” stands for students.

World.title: Global wars are delaying FTA talks, accounting for one-fifth of India’s trade
World.content:
The ongoing wars in the world have led to various degrees of delays in the negotiations of at least three separate trade deals that India is working on, sources in the government have confirmed. These deals involve countries that cumulatively account for about 20% of India’s total trade.

These negotiations are on separate FTAs with the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries, Israel, and the Russia-led Eurasian Economic Union.

“The GCC team had come to Delhi for the signing of the Terms of Reference (ToR) of the deal and so it is our turn to go there for the round of negotiation,” a senior official in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry told The Hindu. “But with all this happening [the ongoing war in West Asia], that visit is pending.”

Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and the Secretary General of the GCC, Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi, on February 24, 2026, formally launched negotiations for a free trade agreement (FTA) between India and the GCC countries — Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

Also Read : Maturing approach: On the India-U.K. Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement

However, later that month, the U.S. launched its attack on Iran. As a result, the first round of negotiations is yet to take place.

“This FTA is of particular importance for India not just as a strategic one, but also because of access,” the official said. “It will mean that any one of the ports of the GCC countries will give India exporters access to all the other countries.”

The negotiations regarding the India-Israel FTA, too, are facing similar delays. The ToR for the deal was signed in Tel Aviv in November 2025 by Mr. Goyal and Israel’s Economy Minister Nir Barkat. The first round of negotiations took place in February 2026 in New Delhi and the second round was to be in May in Tel Aviv.

However, the war in the region delayed these talks as well and changed the location. Talks have only now resumed, with the Israeli negotiation team currently in New Delhi until July 23 to discuss the deal.

“Our team was to go there, but safety was obviously an issue,” the official explained.

He added that similar concerns are leading to delays in India’s in-person negotiations with the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) as well. The EAEU comprises Russia, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Belarus and Armenia.

“The first round of the EAEU FTA was held in November 2025 and the second round in Moscow was held all the way in June 2026,” he explained. “The back-end talks are progressing well, but actual visits are becoming difficult to coordinate especially now that Ukraine has intensified its counteroffensive.”

India conducts $60.7 billion worth of annual trade with the EAEU nations, predominantly with Russia. It has a total annual trade of about $178.7 billion with the GCC countries and $3.9 billion with Israel.

In total, therefore, the wars are delaying negotiations on trade deals involving about $243 billion worth of trade for India, or about 20% of India’s total trade.

World.title: Hundreds of people order food online for protestors at Jantar Mantar
World.content:
Outside the layers of barricades of the Jantar Mantar protest site of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), at the intersection of Tolstoy Marg and Sansad Marg, Aayu Jacob, 18, stopped his blue-coloured motorcycle for the 20th time since Tuesday (July 21, 2026) morning.

“Since morning, I have done 20 rounds here to deliver pizzas. Out of that, four orders were from the U.S. Other delivery agents from our restaurant are also coming here,” Mr. Jacob said.

Every few minutes, a new delivery person stopped at the intersection to deliver food to the protest site, but to no particular person.

The food was being ordered by hundreds of people across the country, with the location as Jantar Mantar protest site and instructions to give the food to the protestors. The food items ranged from pizzas, burgers, momos, to thaalis.

Mr. Jacob said that one of the orders they got on Tuesday to deliver at the site was a single order of 80 pizzas. “Even our manager came to deliver here today, because there were too many orders and we could not manage it,” he said, adding that a few people asked to send a photo or video as proof.

Meanwhile, a person took the delivery and promised to give the pizzas to people at the protest site, and talked to the person who ordered it, via Mr. Jacob’s phone, “You are doing a good job. You are from Bihar? My friend is also from Bihar, talk to him.”

The person who ordered told The Hindu that though he was from Bihar, he was currently studying nursing in Bangalore. “I had also written NEET in the past and then also the question paper got leaked. I later gave it up and took up nursing. I can’t come there now, but I wanted to show support to the students protesting and that is why I ordered pizzas,” the person said over the phone.

Govind, 24, who came on his bike to deliver food, said that he has made 18 trips so far. “The orders ranged from 10 cups of chai to 34 burgers to 200 samosas. I send photos to some people of the food being distributed,” he said.

Mr. Govind, who goes by only first name, said that some people had asked to deliver the food inside the protest site. “I got only 20 rupees for that order, but it took one hour to deliver the food inside and come back. But I still did it. I felt happy to distribute food inside for the students. I also have two children and these people are protesting for the right cause,” he said.

Shahroz Akbar, 42, who stopped to deliver his sixth order, gave the momos to a person at the area, who promised to distribute it. The delivery instruction on the food delivery app on his phone read, “Please offer this to anyone at the jantar mantar protest site.”

Mr. Akbar showed on his phone that there is another delivery he has just got to the protest site itself. Another delivery agent next to him stopped with a delivery of burgers a person had ordered from abroad.

Ayush Rai, a volunteer at the protest site, said that he and his brother have been bringing food from the intersection to the protest site for hours and now there are not many takers.

With so many people ordering food online and many more individuals bringing food physically to the protest site with them, even distributing it was becoming difficult by 10 p.m.

This forced the CJP to post on social media at night asking people not to order any more food online to the protest site. “India is such a beautiful country with such beautiful people - thanks for sending food for protesters. We are so overwhelmed. BUT for today, we have received more than enough food - please don’t send any more!” CJP official handle posted on X at 10:55 p.m.

World.title: Pellet guns, shock batons used against protesters in Delhi; police deny
World.content:
At least one of the 80 protesters injured in police action during the Monday (July 20, 2026) march to Parliament called by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) sustained pellet gun injuries, according to a source at Lady Hardinge Medical College, where the victim is undergoing treatment.

Also read | March to Parliament: Protesters’ anger extends beyond paper leaks

A friend of Shaikh Irshad Mansoori (25), the protester, told The Hindu that Mr. Mansoori was hit near Palika Bazaar in Connaught Place by a Rapid Action Force (RAF) jawan in uniform.

This appears to be the first known instance of security forces using pellet guns on civilians in Delhi. A video of a woman being stunned by a shock baton also emerged on Tuesday (July 21). This is also the first known case of shock batons, which emanate mild electric shock, being used in Delhi.

Pellet guns and shock batons are part of the RAF’s gear, the anti-riot unit under the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), which was deployed alongside Delhi Police on Monday (July 20) in and around Jantar Mantar during the protest demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

While the CRPF did not comment, in response to a video shared by CJP’s Saurav Das on X showing Mr. Mansoori’s wounds, Deputy Commissioner of Police, New Delhi, said, “Reports claiming that police forces are using pellet guns against peaceful protesters are completely false and misleading. The public is strongly advised not to share or circulate unverified content. Please verify facts from official sources before posting or forwarding any information.”

Also Read : The ‘non-lethal’ pellet

Used against farmers

The pellets fired from guns, which penetrate the skin when sprayed from a distance, were last known to have been used during the 2024 farmers’ protest at Khanauri and Shambhu border along the Punjab-Haryana boundary. Though the police had denied the use of pellet guns then, farm leaders had alleged that several persons were injured. In 2023, the guns were used against protesters in ethnic-strife torn Manipur leading to a huge public outrage. In the past, pellet guns have been used in Jammu & Kashmir during the 2016 unrest leaving several people partially or fully blind.

When protest meets crackdown: Cockroach Janta Party protest in pictures 1 / 3

More injuries

During the day, Mr. Mansoori underwent surgery to remove the pellets lodged in the upper part his body. “His surgery was successful and the pellets below his eyes were removed, but one in his neck could not be removed as it was close to a blood vessel. He might require another surgery for the same,” the source said.

According to a source at the hospital, the number of injured increased through the evening and went up to 83, which included both civilians and police officers. The source added that another protester was shifted to AIIMS with an eye injury, which was also likely due to pellets. A protester, aged 15, who sustained other injuries, was shifted to Kalawati Saran Children’s Hospital.

At noon on Tuesday (July 21), Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda visited the hospital and met Mr. Mansoori. A friend who was signing off on his hospital consent forms said, “There are around 30-40 injuries on his face and all over his body. According to doctors, four of them, including one in the neck, penetrated deeply, which is why he is undergoing surgery.”

Originally from Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh, Mr. Mansoori works at a private company in Gurugram and was attending the protests in solidarity. He had some visa-related work in New Delhi, which he was supposed to finish after the protest on Monday (July 20).

The friend added that when Mr. Nadda visited the hospital and asked him why he was at the protest venue, Mr. Mansoori told him that “issues in the education system” had brought him there.

Other than Mr. Mansoori, a 21-year-old woman, Sakshi, who was severely injured in police action, was admitted in a critical condition at the intensive care unit of Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital. Her family members said she was conscious and in better condition than a day ago. Doctors declined to comment on the nature of her injuries.

World.title: U.S. readies new tariffs as Trump's 10% global levy to expire
World.content:
The United States is set to impose new tariffs that could hit dozens of countries soon, trade envoy Jamieson Greer signalled on Tuesday (July 21, 2026), with President Donald Trump's temporary global levies due to expire this week.

The Trump administration has prepared fresh tariffs targeting 60 trading partners over their alleged failures to act against forced labor, as officials push to rebuild the U.S. leader's trade agenda after legal setbacks.

"We expect to see some action soon," Mr. Greer told CNBC when asked if new duties were incoming. He did not specify a timeline.

Mr. Trump imposed a 10% global duty this year after a swath of his tariffs were struck down by the Supreme Court in February, but this levy expires on Friday (July 24, 2026).

Analysts expect that new tariffs over forced labour concerns — set between 10% and 12.5% — would replace these temporary duties.

They come as Mr. Trump makes a renewed push to use tariffs as leverage against U.S. trading partners, sparking fears of retaliation and diplomatic tensions.

Washington announced a fresh 25% duty on certain Brazilian goods last week, and on Monday unveiled a 50-percent levy on many Canadian products to take effect in 30 days.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Tuesday (July 21, 2026) that he was looking at "all options," adding that he and Mr. Trump had agreed to "intensify discussions" in the coming weeks on a possible deal.

On Tuesday (July 21, 2026), Mr. Trump announced a new 100% sector-specific tariff on imported generic drugs to take effect from August 2028, with that level rising to 200% in 2029.

For now, the U.S. leader said the tariff on generic drugs would be cut to zero from August 2026, in an effort to build a window for the onshoring of such pharmaceutical production to the United States.

Forced labor concerns

Mr. Greer said on Tuesday (July 21, 2026) that new action on forced labour will cover the majority of U.S. trade, with the moves likely to reignite trade tensions.

A 10% tariff rate would hit U.S. imports from partners including Canada, the European Union, Mexico, Taiwan and the United Kingdom. They were found to have taken steps against forced labor.

Goods from over 40 other major economies like China, India and Japan face a 12.5% levy.

The EU previously said that it considers tariffs imposed on these grounds "unjustified."

Canada pressure

Washington's planned 50% tariff on Canada also comes as U.S.-Mexico talks over a North American free trade pact intensify.

Washington recently declined to extend the accord in its current form.

Mr. Greer is set to travel to Mexico from Wednesday (July 22, 2026) to Friday (July 24, 2026) for discussions linked to a joint review of the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA).

But negotiations with Canada have proceeded at a slower pace. Carney on Tuesday (July 21, 2026) did not suggest that he would head to Washington for talks.

Some lawyers see Mr. Trump's use of an untested legal provision — Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 — as a means to gain leverage over Canada in USMCA negotiations.

Trade lawyer Dave Townsend of Dorsey & Whitney added that higher tariffs "appear to be aimed at encouraging an agreement between Canada and the United States, or in retaliation for the failure to reach such agreement, or both."

The question, he said, is whether both sides will start a "cycle of escalation and retaliation."

Crucially, Mr. Trump's latest salvo will not exempt affected Canadian products entering his country under the USMCA.

Mr. Trump told reporters on Tuesday (July 21, 2026) that the Canada tariffs were unrelated to his earlier threats over wildfire smoke that descended into the United States.

Brazil tensions

U.S. plans for a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods over accusations of unfair trade practices have separately drawn a sharp rebuke from the Latin American giant.

The levy is due to take effect on Wednesday (July 22, 2026), while shaping up as a major campaign flashpoint just months before Brazil's presidential election.

A range of products like beef, coffee and certain aircraft parts will be exempted, as will some goods that the United States does not produce.

Still, the American Chamber of Commerce for Brazil recently warned that Washington's measure places Brazil among countries "facing the most restrictive conditions for access to the U.S. market," affecting more than $11 billion in exports.

World.title: Jantar Mantar CJP Protest Live Updates: Congress workers protest nationwide against Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi’s detention
World.content:
As the Opposition stepped up the pressure on the government following the alleged atrocities against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protestors, protests erupted nationwide against the detention of Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi, and others on Tuesday.

Congress leaders and youths carried out protest in Assam, Kerala, West Bengal, Jammu and Kashmir, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Haryana, Jharkhand, and other states.
